```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from amab_process import adequacy as ad

DOC = "PCR-006"
UO = "viral_inactivation"
UO_TITLE = "Low-pH Viral Inactivation (Step 6)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- formatting
MINUS = "−"


def fx(x, nd=2):
    """A value with nd decimals, a true minus sign and no negative zero."""
    s = f"{float(x):.{nd}f}"
    if float(s) == 0:
        s = s.lstrip("-")
    return s.replace("-", MINUS)


def g(x):
    return f"{float(x):g}".replace("-", MINUS)


def pfmt(p):
    """A p-value in a table."""
    return "< 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}"


def s3(x):
    """Three significant figures, a true minus sign."""
    return f"{float(x):.3g}".replace("-", MINUS)


def pv(p):
    """A p-value inside a sentence."""
    return "p < 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"p = {p:.3f}"


def rg(lo, hi):
    return f"{g(lo)}–{g(hi)}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- parameters
_uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
FAC = list(D.rsm_factors(UO))                     # the three factors of both designs
PK = FAC + ["protein_conc"]
NAME = {k: _uo.param(k).name for k in PK}
UNIT = {k: _uo.param(k).unit for k in PK}
nm = {k: (NAME[k] if NAME[k][:2].isupper() or NAME[k].startswith("A-Mab") else NAME[k][0].lower() + NAME[k][1:])
      for k in PK}
SP = {k: float(_uo.param(k).setpoint) for k in PK}
NOR = {k: tuple(float(v) for v in _uo.param(k).nor) for k in PK}
RNG = {k: tuple(float(v) for v in _uo.param(k).prange) for k in PK}
with D.characterized_nor():
    _uc = CFG.unit_op(UO)
    SPc = {k: float(_uc.param(k).setpoint) for k in PK}
    NORc = {k: tuple(float(v) for v in _uc.param(k).nor) for k in PK}


def wu(k, txt):
    return f"pH {txt}" if UNIT[k] == "pH" else f"{txt} {UNIT[k]}"


nor_t = {k: wu(k, rg(*NOR[k])) for k in PK}
norc_t = {k: wu(k, rg(*NORc[k])) for k in PK}
rng_t = {k: wu(k, rg(*RNG[k])) for k in PK}
sp_t = {k: wu(k, g(SP[k])) for k in PK}
spc_t = {k: wu(k, g(SPc[k])) for k in PK}
NOR_CHANGE = {k: T.nor_change(_uo.param(k)) for k in FAC}
assert NOR_CHANGE == {"ph": "moved", "hold_time": "narrowed", "temperature": "narrowed"}
assert [k for k in FAC if SP[k] != SPc[k]] == ["ph", "hold_time"]
assert NOR["protein_conc"] == NORc["protein_conc"] == RNG["protein_conc"]
CLASS = report_params(UO).set_index("Parameter")["Class"].to_dict()
CLS = {k: CLASS[NAME[k]] for k in PK}
assert CLS == {"ph": "CPP", "hold_time": "WC-CPP", "temperature": "WC-CPP", "protein_conc": "GPP"}
LET = D.factor_letters(UO)
CENTRE = {k: (RNG[k][0] + RNG[k][1]) / 2 for k in FAC}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- designs and data
n_scr, n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "screening"), doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
c_scr, c_rsm = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening"), doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
SCR = csv(f"doe_{UO}_screening.csv")
RSM = csv(f"doe_{UO}_rsm.csv")
n_fac_scr = int((SCR.run_type == "factorial").sum())
n_fac_rsm = int((RSM.run_type == "factorial").sum())
n_ax = int((RSM.run_type == "axial").sum())
assert n_fac_scr + c_scr == n_scr and n_fac_rsm + n_ax + c_rsm == n_rsm
assert not D.has_augmentation(UO) and not D.setting_corrections(UO, "rsm")
assert SCR[["aggregate_out_pct", "xmulv_lrf", "acidic_variants", "lmw_sec_pct"]].notna().all().all()
assert RSM[["aggregate_out_pct", "xmulv_lrf", "acidic_variants", "lmw_sec_pct", "lmw_cesds_pct"]].notna().all().all()
assert SCR["lmw_cesds_pct"].isna().all()
assert all(not np.isclose(CENTRE[k], SPc[k]) for k in FAC)        # the design centre is no set-point

TH = THRESHOLDS
ALPHA = float(TH["effect_alpha"])
GAPMAX = float(TH["max_r2_minus_pred_r2"])
LOFA = float(TH["lof_alpha"])
RALPHA = float(TH["residual_alpha"])
COOKF = float(TH["cook_factor"])
cook_lim = COOKF / n_rsm
PI = int(round(100 * D.PI_LEVEL))
VB = int(round(100 * float(D.VERIFICATION_BOUND)))
OFFCI = int(round(100 * float(CFG.raw()["analytics"]["sdm"].get("offset_ci", 0.90))))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- criteria
ACC = {r: D.effective_acceptance(UO, r) for r in ["aggregate_out_pct", "xmulv_lrf", "acidic_variants", "lmw_cesds_pct"]}
crit_agg = ACC["aggregate_out_pct"][1]
claim = ACC["xmulv_lrf"][0]
acid_lo, acid_hi = ACC["acidic_variants"][:2]
crit_frag = ACC["lmw_cesds_pct"][1]
IACT = D.iac_table(UO).set_index("response")
agg_apriori = float(IACT.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "iac_high_apriori"])
assert bool(IACT.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "tightened"]) and not IACT["widened"].astype(bool).any()
assert not IACT.drop("aggregate_out_pct")["tightened"].astype(bool).any()
ds_agg = float(IACT.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "ds_high"])
ds_frag = float(IACT.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "ds_high"])
cex_fold_agg = float(IACT.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "downstream_fold"])
cex_fold_frag = float(IACT.loc["lmw_cesds_pct", "downstream_fold"])
_iac_all = D.iac_table().set_index(["step_key", "response"])
claim_aex = float(_iac_all.loc[("aex", "xmulv_lrf"), "iac_low"])
claim_vf = float(_iac_all.loc[("virus_filtration", "xmulv_lrf"), "iac_low"])
xmulv_req = float(IACT.loc["xmulv_lrf", "ds_low"])
claims_sum = claim + claim_aex + claim_vf
assert claims_sum >= xmulv_req
brx_agg = _iac_all.loc[("bioreactor", "aggregates_hmw")]
R1 = D.rev1_criteria(UO).set_index("response")
agg_v1 = float(R1.loc["aggregate_out_pct", "high"])
xmulv_v1 = float(R1.loc["xmulv_lrf", "low"])
assert agg_v1 < crit_agg and xmulv_v1 < claim

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the selected models
RESP = ["aggregate_out_pct", "xmulv_lrf", "acidic_variants", "lmw_cesds_pct"]
FIT = {r: D.fit(UO, "rsm", r) for r in RESP}
RI = {r: D.residual_influence(UO, r) for r in RESP}
A, X, AC, FR = RESP
assert FIT[A]["status"] == "selected" and FIT[X]["status"] == "selected"
assert FIT[AC]["status"] == "none" and FIT[AC]["exact"]
assert FIT[FR]["status"] == "none" and not FIT[FR]["exact"]
assert all(FIT[r]["transform"] is None for r in RESP) and all(FIT[r]["n"] == n_rsm for r in RESP)
assert FIT[A]["names"] == ["hold_time", "temperature"] and FIT[X]["names"] == FAC
assert FIT[AC]["names"] == ["hold_time"]
BC = {r: FIT[r]["boxcox"] for r in (A, X, FR)}
assert all(b["lo"] <= 0 <= b["hi"] and b["lo"] <= 1 <= b["hi"] for b in BC.values())
assert FIT[AC]["boxcox"] is None
for r in (A, X):
    assert FIT[r]["p"] < ALPHA and FIT[r]["p_lof"] >= LOFA and FIT[r]["gap"] <= GAPMAX
    assert RI[r]["met"] and RI[r]["trends_met"] and RI[r]["cook_met"] and RI[r]["over"] and not RI[r]["over_f"]
assert FIT[FR]["p"] < ALPHA and FIT[FR]["p_lof"] >= LOFA and FIT[FR]["gap"] > GAPMAX
assert RI[FR]["met"] and not RI[AC]["testable"]
F_Q = int(round(100 * float(RI[A]["f_quantile"])))
N_SUB = len(ad.hierarchical_subsets(FAC))
N_FULL_TERMS = len(ad.full_terms(FAC))


def term_name(t):
    if ":" in t:
        a_, b_ = t.split(":")
        return f"{nm[a_]} × {nm[b_]}"
    if t.endswith("^2"):
        return nm[t[:-2]] + "²"
    return nm[t]


def terms_text(ts):
    return join_and([term_name(t) for t in ts]) if ts else "no term"


CO = {r: D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, r).set_index("Term") for r in (A, X)}
EFX = {k: 2 * float(CO[X].loc[LET[k], "Coef."]) for k in FAC}
PX = {k: float(CO[X].loc[LET[k], "p-value"]) for k in FAC}
EFA = {k: 2 * float(CO[A].loc[LET[k], "Coef."]) for k in ("hold_time", "temperature")}
PA = {k: float(CO[A].loc[LET[k], "p-value"]) for k in ("hold_time", "temperature")}
assert EFX["ph"] < 0 < EFX["temperature"] < EFX["hold_time"] and abs(EFX["ph"]) > EFX["hold_time"]
assert 0 < EFA["temperature"] < EFA["hold_time"]
# the full quadratic (the plan's model) bounds a pH term in aggregate
_fq_a = D.fit(UO, "rsm", A, form="full", runs="planned")["model"]
_ci = _fq_a.conf_int(alpha=ALPHA).loc["ph"]
agg_ph_lo, agg_ph_hi = 2 * float(_ci.iloc[0]), 2 * float(_ci.iloc[1])
assert agg_ph_lo < 0 < agg_ph_hi
_fq_x = D.fit(UO, "rsm", X, form="full", runs="planned")["model"]
_ci = _fq_x.conf_int(alpha=ALPHA).loc["ph:hold_time"]
x_ab_lo, x_ab_hi = 2 * float(_ci.iloc[0]), 2 * float(_ci.iloc[1])
x_ab_p = float(_fq_x.pvalues["ph:hold_time"])
assert x_ab_p >= ALPHA

# acidic variants: one value per hold time, in both designs
_both = pd.concat([SCR, RSM], ignore_index=True)
_ab = _both.groupby("hold_time")["acidic_variants"].agg(["min", "max"])
assert np.allclose(_ab["min"], _ab["max"]) and len(_ab) == 3
ACID_T = {float(k): float(v) for k, v in _ab["min"].items()}
acid_rise = ACID_T[RNG["hold_time"][1]] - ACID_T[RNG["hold_time"][0]]
acid_per60 = acid_rise / ((RNG["hold_time"][1] - RNG["hold_time"][0]) / 60)
assert acid_rise > 0

# screening effects
SE = {r: D.screening_effects_df(UO, r).set_index("Term") for r in (A, X)}
SCRSIG = {r: [t for t in SE[r].index if SE[r].loc[t, "p-value"] < ALPHA] for r in SE}
SE_AC = D.screening_effects_df(UO, AC).set_index("Term")
assert SCRSIG[A] == ["B", "C"] and SCRSIG[X] == ["A", "B", "C"]
SFS = D.fit_summary_df(UO, "screening").set_index("Response")
LAB = D.RESP_LABEL
# screening against response surface, XMuLV: the same corner settings in both designs
_cmp = {}
for k in FAC:
    e1, s1 = float(SE[X].loc[LET[k], "Effect"]), 2 * float(SE[X].loc[LET[k], "Std. err."])
    e2, s2 = EFX[k], 2 * float(CO[X].loc[LET[k], "Std. err."])
    z = (e1 - e2) / np.hypot(s1, s2)
    _cmp[k] = dict(scr=e1, rsm=e2, z=z, p=float(2 * sstat.norm.sf(abs(z))))
_cs = SCR[SCR.run_type == "factorial"].set_index(FAC)["xmulv_lrf"]
_cr = RSM[RSM.run_type == "factorial"].set_index(FAC)["xmulv_lrf"]
_dc = (_cs - _cr.reindex(_cs.index))
d_low_ph = float(_dc[_dc.index.get_level_values("ph") == RNG["ph"][0]].mean())
d_high_ph = float(_dc[_dc.index.get_level_values("ph") == RNG["ph"][1]].mean())
CVR = D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm").set_index("Response")
CVS = D.center_cv_df(UO, "screening").set_index("Response")
d_centre = float(CVS.loc[LAB[X], "Mean"] - CVR.loc[LAB[X], "Mean"])
sd_pe_x = float(np.sqrt(FIT[X]["ss_pe"] / FIT[X]["df_pe"]))
assert _cmp["ph"]["p"] < ALPHA and _cmp["hold_time"]["p"] >= ALPHA and _cmp["temperature"]["p"] >= ALPHA
assert d_low_ph > 0 and d_centre > 0 and abs(d_high_ph) < sd_pe_x
_fr_c = RSM[RSM.run_type == "center"]["lmw_cesds_pct"]
fr_c_mean, fr_c_sd = float(_fr_c.mean()), float(_fr_c.std(ddof=1))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the model search
SC = D.selection_comparison()
_scx = SC[~SC["exact"].astype(bool)]
n_sc = len(_scx)
n_sc_back = int(_scx["backward_worse"].astype(bool).sum())
n_sc_any = int((_scx["backward_worse"].astype(bool) | _scx["forward_worse"].astype(bool)).sum())
_scv = _scx[_scx.step_key == UO].set_index("response")
assert bool(_scv.loc[A, "backward_worse"]) and not bool(_scv.loc[A, "forward_worse"])
assert not bool(_scv.loc[X, "backward_worse"]) and not bool(_scv.loc[X, "forward_worse"])
assert bool(_scv.loc[FR, "backward_worse"]) and bool(_scv.loc[FR, "forward_worse"])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- judgement over a NOR, doc-local models
def _nor_grid(char=False):
    def _g():
        u = CFG.unit_op(UO)
        lv = [[u.param(f).nor[0], u.param(f).setpoint, u.param(f).nor[1]] for f in FAC]
        gg = list(itertools.product(*lv))
        return {f: [x[i] for x in gg] for i, f in enumerate(FAC)}
    if char:
        with D.characterized_nor():
            return _g()
    return _g()


def _coded(nat):
    return pd.DataFrame({"coded_" + f: np.atleast_1d(D.to_coded(UO, f, np.asarray(nat[f], float))) for f in FAC})


def _pred(model, terms, nat, alpha):
    sf = model.get_prediction(ad.matrix(_coded(nat), terms, False)).summary_frame(alpha=alpha)
    return sf["mean"].to_numpy(), sf["obs_ci_lower"].to_numpy(), sf["obs_ci_upper"].to_numpy()


off_agg = D.sdm_offset(UO, A)
off_acid = D.sdm_offset(UO, AC)


def judge(resp, model, terms, char=False):
    """The judgement of PCMP-001 over a NOR for a model of this report's own: aggregate on the upper
    end of the single-run prediction interval at manufacturing scale, XMuLV on the lowest mean."""
    mu, lo, hi = _pred(model, terms, _nor_grid(char), 1 - D.PI_LEVEL)
    if resp == X:
        return float(mu.min()), bool(mu.min() >= claim)
    v = float((hi - off_agg["offset"]).max())
    return v, bool(v <= crit_agg)


PLANNED = D.rsm_data(UO, "planned")
FEED_AGG = None
_ps = csv("process_summary.csv")
_ps6 = _ps[_ps.step == _uo.step].iloc[0]
FEED_AGG = float(_ps6["aggregate_out_pct"] - _ps6["aggregate_delta_pct"])


def agg_bound(model, terms):
    """The verification bound of the aggregate increase: the one-sided upper prediction bound of a
    single run at the combination of the NOR as characterized with the largest predicted increase,
    minus the load level of the nominal batch of the step model."""
    mu, lo, hi = _pred(model, terms, _nor_grid(char=True), 2 * (1 - float(D.VERIFICATION_BOUND)))
    i = int(np.argmax(mu))
    return float(mu[i] - FEED_AGG), float(hi[i] - FEED_AGG)


VV = D.iac_verification(UO).set_index("cqa")
v_agg, v_frag, v_acid = VV.loc["aggregates_hmw"], VV.loc["fragments_lmw"], VV.loc["acidic_variants"]
_pa, _ba = agg_bound(FIT[A]["model"], FIT[A]["names"])
assert np.isclose(_pa, v_agg["predicted_nor"], atol=1e-3) and np.isclose(_ba, v_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"], atol=1e-3)
assert bool(v_agg["met"]) and bool(v_agg["widening_supported"]) and bool(v_agg["model_adequate"])
assert v_agg["observed_edge"] > v_agg["assumed"] > v_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"]
assert v_acid["observed_edge"] < v_acid["assumed"] and not bool(v_acid["model_adequate"])
assert v_frag["observed_edge"] > v_frag["assumed"] and not bool(v_frag["model_adequate"])
assert v_frag["predicted_nor_bound95"] > v_frag["assumed"]
# the bound over the NOR as characterized also covers the NOR in force (no pH term, same longest
# hold and highest temperature)
_mu_c, _, _hi_c = _pred(FIT[A]["model"], FIT[A]["names"], _nor_grid(True), 0.10)
_mu_f, _, _hi_f = _pred(FIT[A]["model"], FIT[A]["names"], _nor_grid(False), 0.10)
assert np.isclose(_hi_c.max(), _hi_f.max()) and "ph" not in FIT[A]["names"]
assert NOR["hold_time"][1] == NORc["hold_time"][1] and NOR["temperature"][1] == NORc["temperature"][1]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- near-equivalent models
def near_models(resp):
    r = FIT[resp]
    d = r["df"]
    y = d[r["ycol"]].to_numpy(float)
    rows = []
    for ts in ad.hierarchical_subsets(FAC):
        rows.append((ad.aicc(y, ad.matrix(d, ts, False).to_numpy(float)), ts))
    best = min(a for a, _ in rows)
    out = []
    for a, ts in sorted(rows, key=lambda x: x[0]):
        if a - best > 2.0:
            break
        m = sm.OLS(y, ad.matrix(d, ts, False)).fit()
        q = ad.adequacy(d, r["ycol"], FAC, ts, D.TH)
        crit13 = bool(q["adequate"] and (not ts or q["p"] < ALPHA))
        if resp == FR:
            _, _, hi = _pred(m, ts, _nor_grid(), 1 - D.PI_LEVEL)
            val, met = float(hi.max()), bool(hi.max() <= crit_frag)
        else:
            val, met = judge(resp, m, ts)
        out.append(dict(resp=resp, d_aicc=a - best, terms=ts, gap=q["gap"], crit13=crit13, value=val, met=met))
    return out


NEAR = {r: near_models(r) for r in (A, X, FR)}
assert all(n["met"] and n["crit13"] for r in (A, X) for n in NEAR[r])
NEAR_FR_OK = [n for n in NEAR[FR] if n["crit13"]]
assert len(NEAR_FR_OK) == 1 and NEAR_FR_OK[0]["terms"] == ["hold_time"] and NEAR_FR_OK[0]["met"]
assert not NEAR[FR][0]["crit13"]

# ------------------------------------------------- the examination of a flagged run (PCP-006 §7.1)
def influence(resp):
    rows = []
    for run in RI[resp]["over"]:
        rest = PLANNED[PLANNED["run"] != run].reset_index(drop=True)
        sel = ad.select_model(rest, resp, FAC, D.TH)
        val, met = judge(resp, sel["model"], sel["terms"])
        row = dict(resp=resp, run=run, cook=float(RI[resp]["cook"][RI[resp]["runs"].index(run)]),
                   terms=list(sel["terms"]), adequate=bool(sel["adequate"]), value=val, met=met)
        if resp == A:
            row["bound"] = agg_bound(sel["model"], sel["terms"])[1]
        else:
            row["value_char"], row["met_char"] = judge(resp, sel["model"], sel["terms"], char=True)
        rows.append(row)
    return rows


INF = {r: influence(r) for r in (A, X)}
assert all(i["adequate"] and i["met"] for r in (A, X) for i in INF[r])
assert all(i["bound"] < v_agg["assumed"] for i in INF[A])
assert all(not i["met_char"] for i in INF[X])
TREND = {}
for r in (A, X):
    fv = FIT[r]["model"].fittedvalues
    TREND[r] = dict(order=RI[r]["order_slope"] * RI[r]["order_range"], p_order=RI[r]["p_order"],
                    spread=RI[r]["spread_slope"] * float(fv.max() - fv.min()), p_spread=RI[r]["p_spread"])
assert all(abs(TREND[r]["order"]) < FIT[r]["rmse"] for r in (A, X))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- judgement over the NOR, both NORs
WC_X = D.nor_worst_corner(UO, X)
WC_A = D.nor_worst_corner(UO, A)
UPL_A = D.nor_prediction_limit(UO, A)
MET = {r: D.nor_met(UO, r) for r in RESP}
with D.characterized_nor():
    WC_Xc = D.nor_worst_corner(UO, X)
    METc = {r: D.nor_met(UO, r) for r in RESP}
    PTc = D.par_table(UO)
    QUALc = {r: D.offset_qualification(UO, r)["qualified"] for r in (A, AC)}
assert all(MET.values()) and METc[X] is False and all(METc[r] for r in (A, AC, FR))
assert WC_X["median_met"] and not WC_Xc["median_met"]
assert all(QUALc.values())
X_SPC = D.prediction_interval(UO, X, {k: [SPc[k]] for k in FAC})
X_SP = float(D.predict(UO, X, natural={k: SP[k] for k in FAC})[0])
_xc = PTc[PTc["CQA"] == LAB[X]]
assert (_xc["PAR (NOR)"] == "none (set-point breaches)").all()
MEAS = {r: D.to_mfg(UO, r, D.measured_values(UO, r)) for r in RESP}
x_below = int((MEAS[X] < claim).sum())
assert x_below > 0 and D.measured_met(UO, X) is False
assert MEAS[FR].max() <= crit_frag and MEAS[AC].min() >= acid_lo and MEAS[AC].max() <= acid_hi
# with the offset at either end of its interval
with D.offset_at("lo"):
    _acl = D.to_mfg(UO, AC, D.measured_values(UO, AC))
with D.offset_at("hi"):
    _ach = D.to_mfg(UO, AC, D.measured_values(UO, AC))
assert _acl.min() >= acid_lo and _ach.min() >= acid_lo and _acl.max() <= acid_hi and _ach.max() <= acid_hi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- PARs
PT = D.par_table(UO)


def _par(resp, k, col="PAR (NOR)"):
    return PT[(PT["CQA"] == LAB.get(resp, resp)) & (PT["Parameter"] == NAME[k])][col].iloc[0]


def _edges(s):

    if c >= CPK_TARGET:

    if c >= CPK_MIN:

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the pH edge of the claim
def ph_edge(hold_low, temp_low):
    """The inactivation pH at which the mean predicted log reduction falls to the claim, with the
    hold time and the temperature at the given ends of their NOR, which is where the claim is least
    favourable. The two factors raise the log reduction, so the lowest mean over a NOR sits at their
    low ends."""
    r = FIT[X]
    xs = np.linspace(RNG["ph"][0], RNG["ph"][1], 20001)
    y = D.predict(UO, X, natural={"ph": xs, "hold_time": np.full(xs.size, hold_low),
                                  "temperature": np.full(xs.size, temp_low)})
    i = int(np.argmin(np.abs(y - claim)))
    return float(xs[i])

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- revision 1: the decision stages
def par_wc(pred, factor, nor, sp):
    """The PAR of `factor` for XMuLV clearance as the engine computes it (``par_nor_propagated``,
    worst-case branch): 81 grid points over the range studied, the other two factors at every
    combination of their NOR low, set-point and NOR high, the lowest mean prediction against the
    claim, contiguous around the set-point. ``pred`` maps natural settings to mean predictions, so
    the same rule can be applied at the NOR of each decision stage and to a refitted model."""
    xs = np.linspace(RNG[factor][0], RNG[factor][1], D.PAR_GRID)
    others = [f for f in FAC if f != factor]
    combos = list(itertools.product(*[[nor[o][0], sp[o], nor[o][1]] for o in others]))
    ok = []
    for x in xs:
        nat = {factor: np.full(len(combos), x)}
        for i, o in enumerate(others):
            nat[o] = np.array([c[i] for c in combos])
        ok.append(bool(np.min(pred(nat)) >= claim))
    ok = np.array(ok)
    ci = int(np.argmin(np.abs(xs - sp[factor])))
    if not ok[ci]:
        return None
    lo, hi = ci, ci
    while lo > 0 and ok[lo - 1]:
        lo -= 1
    while hi < len(xs) - 1 and ok[hi + 1]:
        hi += 1
    return float(xs[lo]), float(xs[hi])

# hold-time NOR narrowed to the range in force. The stage-2 set-point is one of the hold times of

assert np.isclose(brx_final, ds_agg * float(brx_agg["downstream_fold"]) - float(v_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"]))
assert brx_tight < brx_final < brx_apriori

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- revision 1: what CA3 changed
_fa = D.fit(UO, "rsm", A, form="full", runs="planned")
bound_full = agg_bound(_fa["model"], _fa["names"])[1]
with D.criteria_without_ca3():
    brx_agg_noca3 = D.iac_limit("bioreactor", "aggregates_hmw")[1]
    brx_acid_noca3 = D.iac_limit("bioreactor", "acidic_variants")[1]
brx_acid_ca3 = D.iac_limit("bioreactor", "acidic_variants")[1]
cex_fold_noca3 = agg_wo_ca3 / ds_agg
assert abs(bound_full - float(v_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"])) < 0.01 and brx_agg_noca3 < brx_final
assert brx_acid_noca3 > brx_acid_ca3

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- revision 1: Version 1.0 region
with D.rev1_criteria_in_force():
    DSV1 = D.design_space_grid(UO, basis="mean")
assert DSV1["binding"] == A and DSV1["fraction"] > DSG["fraction"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- revision 1: results at manufacturing scale
_of = OFD[OFD.ph == ph_new]
_of_nor = _of[(_of.hold_min >= NOR["hold_time"][0]) & (_of.hold_min <= NOR["hold_time"][1])]
_of_all = _of[_of.hold_min <= NOR["hold_time"][1]]
OF_MFG = {"nor": dict(agg=D.to_mfg(UO, A, _of_nor[A]), frag=_of_nor[FR].to_numpy(), acid=D.to_mfg(UO, AC, _of_nor[AC])),
          "all": dict(agg=D.to_mfg(UO, A, _of_all[A]), frag=_of_all[FR].to_numpy(), acid=D.to_mfg(UO, AC, _of_all[AC]))}
WC_MFG = dict(agg=D.to_mfg(UO, A, WCW["load_aggregate_pct"]), acid=D.to_mfg(UO, AC, WCW["load_acidic_variants"]),
              frag=WCW["load_lmw_cesds_pct"].to_numpy())
assert OF_MFG["nor"]["agg"].max() <= crit_agg and acid_lo <= OF_MFG["nor"]["acid"].min()
oft_hold_nor = sorted(float(h) for h in _of_nor["hold_min"].unique())

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- revision 1: the concentration studies
_g2 = U2.groupby("level")["aggregate_out_pct"]
u2_agg = {k: float(D.to_mfg(UO, A, v)) for k, v in _g2.mean().items()}
_sd2 = float(np.sqrt(_g2.var(ddof=1).mean()))
_t2 = sstat.t.ppf(0.975, int(_g2.count().sum() - 2))
u2_agg_d = u2_agg["high"] - u2_agg["low"]
u2_agg_lo, u2_agg_hi = u2_agg_d - _t2 * _sd2, u2_agg_d + _t2 * _sd2
assert u2_agg_lo < 0 < u2_agg_hi
_tq = sstat.t.ppf(0.975, u2_df)
u2_x_lo, u2_x_hi = -u2_d - _tq * u2_se, -u2_d + _tq * u2_se          # high minus low
assert u2_x_lo < -(WC_X["predicted"] - claim) < 0 < u2_x_hi           # a loss larger than the margin is not excluded
u1_acid_d = u1_acid - sdm_acid_mean
assert abs(u1_acid_d) < sdm_acid_sd
u1_agg_dev = {k: abs(v - sdm_agg_mean) for k, v in u1_agg.items()}
n_acid_flat = len(SCR) + len(RSM) + len(U1)
assert n_acid_flat == 33
assert sum("ph^2" in n_["terms"] for n_ in NEAR[FR]) == 3 and sum("hold_time^2" in n_["terms"] for n_ in NEAR[FR]) == 2
assert all(("ph^2" in n_["terms"]) == (not n_["crit13"]) for n_ in NEAR[FR])
inf_agg_upper = max(i_["cube_upper"] for i_ in INF[A])

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- revision 2: both margins of each PAR
MARG_OTH = {"ph": NOR["ph"][0] - PE["ph"][0], "hold_time": PE["hold_time"][1] - NOR["hold_time"][1],
            "temperature": PE["temperature"][1] - NOR["temperature"][1]}
_mu_nf, _lo_nf, _hi_nf = _pred(FIT[A]["model"], FIT[A]["names"], _nor_grid(), 1 - D.PI_LEVEL)
PI_LO_A = float((_lo_nf - off_agg["offset"]).min())
PI_HI_A = float((_hi_nf - off_agg["offset"]).max())
assert np.isclose(PI_HI_A, UPL_A) and PI_LO_A < WC_A["pi_low"]
assert np.isclose(PI_LO_A, D.nor_prediction_limit(UO, A, "lower"))
assert np.isclose(PI_HI_A, D.nor_prediction_limit(UO, A, "upper"))
assert all(v > 0 for v in MARG_OTH.values())
assert PE["ph"][0] == RNG["ph"][0] and PE["hold_time"][1] == RNG["hold_time"][1]
assert PE["temperature"][1] == RNG["temperature"][1]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- revision 2: aggregate along the hold time
AGG_H = {h: float(D.to_mfg(UO, A, D.predict(UO, A, natural={"ph": SP["ph"], "hold_time": h,
                                                            "temperature": SP["temperature"]}))[0])
         for h in (RNG["hold_time"][0], SP["hold_time"], RNG["hold_time"][1])}
agg_h_rise = AGG_H[RNG["hold_time"][1]] - AGG_H[RNG["hold_time"][0]]
assert np.isclose(agg_h_rise, EFA["hold_time"], atol=0.01)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- revision 2: fragments against the method
fr_sd = float(OF.loc[FR, "method_sd"])
fr_ratio = fr_rise_range / fr_sd
assert fr_ratio > 1

# ------------------------------------------- revision 2: the temperature effect on aggregate after a deletion
for _i in INF[A]:
    _rest = PLANNED[PLANNED["run"] != _i["run"]].reset_index(drop=True)
    _sel = ad.select_model(_rest, A, FAC, D.TH)
    _i["temp_eff"] = 2 * float(_sel["model"].params["temperature"])
    _i["temp_p"] = float(_sel["model"].pvalues["temperature"])
assert all("temperature" in i_["terms"] and i_["temp_p"] < ALPHA for i_ in INF[A])
agg_temp_lo = min(i_["temp_eff"] for i_ in INF[A])
agg_temp_hi = max(i_["temp_eff"] for i_ in INF[A])
agg_temp_p_max = max(i_["temp_p"] for i_ in INF[A])


# -------------------------------------- revision 2: the fourth criterion for a model near the selected one
def crit4(resp, terms):
    """The fourth criterion of PCMP-001 §7.2 for a model of this report's own, by the rule of PCP-006
    §7.1: the two residual regressions at their level, and the Cook's distance of each run against the
    cut-off for examination and against the F limit at which the model fails."""
    r = FIT[resp]
    d = r["df"]
    y = d[r["ycol"]].to_numpy(float)
    Xm = ad.matrix(d, terms, False)
    m = sm.OLS(y, Xm).fit()
    n_, p_ = len(y), Xm.shape[1]
    rs = np.asarray(m.resid)
    p_spread = float(sm.OLS(np.abs(rs), sm.add_constant(np.asarray(m.fittedvalues))).fit().pvalues[1])
    p_order = float(sm.OLS(rs, sm.add_constant(d["run_order"].to_numpy(float))).fit().pvalues[1])
    ck = m.get_influence().cooks_distance[0]
    flim = float(sstat.f.ppf(float(RI[resp]["f_quantile"]), p_, max(n_ - p_, 1)))
    over = [int(d["run"].iloc[i]) for i in range(n_) if ck[i] > COOKF / n_]
    over_f = [int(d["run"].iloc[i]) for i in range(n_) if ck[i] > flim]
    return dict(p_spread=p_spread, p_order=p_order, over=over, over_f=over_f,
                met=bool(p_spread >= RALPHA and p_order >= RALPHA and not over_f))


for _r in (A, X, FR):               # the same answer as the engine for the selected model
    _c4 = crit4(_r, FIT[_r]["names"])
    assert _c4["met"] == bool(RI[_r]["met"]) and _c4["over"] == list(RI[_r]["over"])
    assert _c4["over_f"] == list(RI[_r]["over_f"]) and np.isclose(_c4["p_spread"], RI[_r]["p_spread"])
    assert np.isclose(_c4["p_order"], RI[_r]["p_order"])
    for n_ in NEAR[_r]:
        n_["crit4"] = crit4(_r, n_["terms"])["met"]
for _r in (A, X, FR):
    for n_ in NEAR[_r]:
        n_["adequate"] = bool(n_["crit13"] and n_["crit4"])
NEAR_C4_FAIL = {_r: [n_ for n_ in NEAR[_r] if not n_["crit4"]] for _r in (A, X, FR)}
assert [len(NEAR_C4_FAIL[_r]) for _r in (A, X, FR)] == [1, 0, 1]
assert NEAR_C4_FAIL[A][0]["terms"] == ["hold_time", "temperature", "hold_time:temperature"]
assert NEAR_C4_FAIL[A][0]["met"] and NEAR_C4_FAIL[A][0]["crit13"]
assert not NEAR_C4_FAIL[FR][0]["crit13"] and NEAR[FR][0]["crit4"]
assert all(n_["adequate"] for n_ in NEAR[X]) and NEAR[A][0]["adequate"]
assert sum(n_["adequate"] for n_ in NEAR[A]) == 2 and sum(n_["adequate"] for n_ in NEAR[FR]) == 1
assert [n_["adequate"] for n_ in NEAR[FR]].index(True) == 2
near_a_run = crit4(A, NEAR_C4_FAIL[A][0]["terms"])["over_f"][0]
assert near_a_run in RI[A]["over"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- revision 2: acidic variants per hold time
acid_u1_hold = SPc["hold_time"]
assert acid_u1_hold not in ACID_T and U1["acidic_variants"].nunique() == 1
ACID_H = dict(ACID_T)
ACID_H[acid_u1_hold] = u1_acid
ACID_H = {k: ACID_H[k] for k in sorted(ACID_H)}
assert len(ACID_H) == 4 and U2["acidic_variants"].nunique() == len(U2)

# ------------------------------------------- revision 2: the held pool beside the study run beside it
h_acid_max = float(H["acidic_pct"].max())
h_d0_raw = sorted(float(v) for v in H[H.day == 0]["acidic_pct"])
h_acid_max_mfg = float(D.to_mfg(UO, AC, pd.Series([h_acid_max]))[0])
h_d0_mfg = sorted(float(v) for v in D.to_mfg(UO, AC, H[H.day == 0]["acidic_pct"]))
of_acid_mfg = D.to_mfg(UO, AC, OFD["acidic_variants"])
assert min(h_d0_mfg) > float(of_acid_mfg.max())       # the held pool starts above every S-VI-OFAT result

assert CHR.loc["S-VI-OFAT", "start"] >= CHR.loc["S-VI-HLD", "start"]

MP = csv("method_plan.csv")
MP = MP[MP.step == UO].set_index("study")
FR_RE = [s for s in RE_STUDIES if s in MP.index and bool(MP.loc[s, "lmw_cesds"])]

assert FR_RE_NOT == ["S-VI-UNI2"] and len(FR_RE) == 3 and len(FR_RE) + 1 + 1 == len(RE_STUDIES)

acid_ds_lo = float(CAPD.loc["acidic_variants", "acc_low"])
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Low-pH viral inactivation is Step 6 of the A-Mab drug substance process. The Protein A eluate is held at acid pH for a set time and then neutralized. The hold inactivates enveloped viruses. The drug substance requires a cumulative clearance of xenotropic murine leukemia virus (XMuLV) of at least `{python} fx(xmulv_req, 1)` log~10~, which three steps claim together, and the claim of this step is `{python} fx(claim)` log~10~ of it. The same conditions can add aggregate, fragments and acidic variants to the pool. This report presents the Stage 1 characterization of the step under its plan PCP-006 and the master plan PCMP-001 [@fda2011]. The studies were run in a scale-down model of the step, qualified for aggregate and acidic variants, and in a small-scale spiking model, at the development site in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION`.

Inactivation pH, hold time and temperature were studied in a screening design of `{python} n_scr` runs and a response-surface design of `{python} n_rsm` runs. A-Mab concentration was studied one factor at a time. These characterization studies ran from `{python} char_start` to `{python} char_end`. `{python} W(len(RE_STUDIES)).capitalize()` further studies were made from `{python} re_start` to `{python} re_end`, during the Version 2.0 re-analysis and after the results of the designs were known. They are registered as discrepancies from the plan (@sec-record). The findings are the following.

F1. At the normal operating ranges (NORs) against which the studies were planned, the XMuLV claim was not met. The lowest mean predicted log reduction was `{python} fx(WC_Xc["predicted"])` log~10~, at `{python} wu("ph", g(WC_Xc["settings"]["ph"]))`, `{python} wu("hold_time", g(WC_Xc["settings"]["hold_time"]))` and `{python} wu("temperature", g(WC_Xc["settings"]["temperature"]))`, against the claim of `{python} fx(claim)` log~10~. The pH set-point and NOR were therefore moved to `{python} sp_t["ph"]` and `{python} nor_t["ph"]`, the hold-time NOR was narrowed to `{python} nor_t["hold_time"]` with its set-point at `{python} sp_t["hold_time"]`, and the temperature NOR was narrowed to `{python} nor_t["temperature"]`. Across the NOR in force the lowest mean predicted log reduction is `{python} fx(WC_X["predicted"])` log~10~, so the claim is met there.

F2. Aggregate, fragments and acidic variants meet their intermediate acceptance criteria across the NOR in force. The upper limit of the 95 % prediction interval of a single batch of aggregate is at most `{python} fx(UPL_A)` % HMW at manufacturing scale, against `{python} fx(crit_agg)` %. Fragments and acidic variants have no adequate model and are judged on their measured results, `{python} fx(MEAS[FR].min())` to `{python} fx(MEAS[FR].max())` % and `{python} fx(MEAS[AC].min(), 1)` to `{python} fx(MEAS[AC].max(), 1)` % respectively. The `{python} n_acid_flat` acidic variant results of the designs and the first concentration study show no scatter at a given hold time, so no adequacy test can be applied to that output.

F3. The selected models of aggregate and of the XMuLV log reduction meet all four model-adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2. `{python} W(len(RI[A]["over"]) + len(RI[X]["over"])).capitalize()` runs carry a Cook's distance above the cut-off at which PCP-006 §7.1 calls for an examination. Each was deleted in turn, the model selected again on the remaining `{python} n_rsm - 1` runs and the output judged over the NOR again. Under every one of those models the NOR in force lies inside the proven acceptable range (PAR) of each factor, the claim is met over the NOR, aggregate keeps its margin to its criterion, the move of the pH NOR remains necessary, and inactivation pH stays a critical process parameter, hold time and temperature well-controlled critical process parameters and A-Mab concentration a general process parameter. With run `{python} INF5["run"]` deleted the temperature term leaves the XMuLV model and the XMuLV ranges widen. Temperature raises aggregate by `{python} fx(agg_temp_lo, 3)` to `{python} fx(agg_temp_hi, 3)` percentage points in every model after a deletion.

F4. The PARs are `{python} wu("ph", PARX["ph"])`, `{python} wu("hold_time", PARX["hold_time"])` and `{python} wu("temperature", PARX["temperature"])`. One edge of each is the setting at which the mean predicted log reduction falls to the claim, and the other is the end of the range studied. The NOR in force lies `{python} fx(MARG["ph"])` pH units inside the upper pH edge, `{python} g(MARG["hold_time"])` min inside the lower hold-time edge and `{python} fx(MARG["temperature"], 1)` °C inside the lower temperature edge, and `{python} fx(MARG_OTH["ph"])` pH units, `{python} g(MARG_OTH["hold_time"])` min and `{python} fx(MARG_OTH["temperature"], 1)` °C inside the three edges that are ends of the range studied.

F5. Inactivation pH was classified as a critical process parameter (CPP). Hold time and temperature were classified as well-controlled critical process parameters (WC-CPPs), and A-Mab concentration as a general process parameter (GPP). For XMuLV clearance the concentration study bounds the effect loosely, with four runs, so the GPP class rests for that attribute on how the hold acts. The acid denatures the envelope of the virus, and the antibody around it neither shields the envelope nor takes part in that reaction.

F6. Within the NOR as characterized the step adds at most `{python} fx(v_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"])` percentage points of aggregate at the one-sided `{python} VB` % prediction bound of a single batch, against the platform value of `{python} fx(v_agg["assumed"])`. That bound moved the aggregate criterion of the production bioreactor output from `{python} fx(brx_tight)` to `{python} fx(brx_final)` % HMW. At a hold of `{python} g(RNG["hold_time"][1])` min, outside the NOR, the step added up to `{python} fx(v_agg["observed_edge"])` points. The platform values for fragments and acidic variants stand.

F7. At the new pH set-point aggregate and fragments showed no effect of pH. Acidic variants were `{python} fx(abs(OF.loc[AC, "ph_effect"]))` percentage points lower at `{python} sp_t["ph"]` than at `{python} spc_t["ph"]`, a significant difference after adjustment (`{python} pv(OF.loc[AC, "p_ph_holm"])`) that was already present before the hold began and that is `{python} fx(abs(OF.loc[AC, "ph_effect"]))` points against a criterion `{python} fx(acid_hi - acid_lo, 1)` points wide. Cation exchange cleared aggregate and fragments from that material as the criteria assume. At the low end of the pH PAR, with hold time and temperature at the upper ends of their NORs, product quality met every criterion of the step and cation exchange cleared aggregate as required. For fragments every run cleared more than the required clearance factor, but the lower confidence bound of the three runs fell below it, so the rule fixed before the runs was not met. That was accepted on its risk, on the grounds PD-006-03 records and @sec-wc gives.

F8. The neutralized pool met its criteria after `{python} H_DAYS` days at `{python} join_and(H_TEMPS)`.

F9. The capability index (Cpk) of cumulative XMuLV clearance is `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["lrv_xmulv", "Cpk"])`, which `{python} cpk_verdict(CAPD.loc["lrv_xmulv", "Cpk"])`. Acidic variants have the lowest Cpk of the attributes this step changes, `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpk"])`, which `{python} cpk_verdict(CAPD.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpk"])`. The lower end of the criterion limits it. The attribute is formed in the production bioreactor, the simulated drug substance mean is `{python} fx(acid_mean, 1)` % with a batch standard deviation of `{python} fx(acid_sd, 1)` points, and the lower limit of the drug substance criterion is `{python} fx(acid_ds_lo, 1)` %. The low-pH hold raises acidic variants, so it moves them away from the limit that binds.

F10. The record of execution holds `{python} W(n_dev)` study events. A hold-time record discrepancy of `{python} g(dev_006_01_time_discrepancy_min)` min between the control system and the manual log (DEV-006-01) changes the predicted log reduction by `{python} fx(dev1_x, 3)` log~10~ and the predicted aggregate by `{python} fx(dev1_a, 3)` percentage points. Cytotoxicity of the infectivity assay at low dilution (DEV-006-02) raises the lowest titre the assay can report, which can only make a computed log reduction smaller. The runs of both events were retained in the analysis. `{python} W(len(PDS)).capitalize()` discrepancies from the plan are registered, `{python} W(len(RE_STUDIES))` of them studies made during the re-analysis (@sec-record).

The ranges, classes and controls of this report roll up into the Process Characterization Master Report PCMR-001.

# Introduction {#sec-intro}

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose drug substance is made by `{python} COMPANY`. It is purified by the Novacyte platform train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, virus filtration and ultrafiltration and diafiltration [@amab2009]. The process is transferred under the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001 from the development site in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION` to the commercial drug substance site in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION`, where it runs at the `{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L scale.

Low-pH viral inactivation follows Protein A capture. The Protein A eluate leaves the column at low pH. It is adjusted to the inactivation pH, held for the hold time at the set temperature and then neutralized with base. The neutralized pool is the load of cation exchange. The step is operated under its standard operating procedure, SOP-2009.

The step contributes one of the three claims that meet the cumulative requirement for clearance of the enveloped model virus XMuLV. The other two claims are those of anion exchange and virus filtration. The step can also add aggregate, fragments and acidic variants, which are formed upstream, so each of them has an intermediate acceptance criterion at the output of this step (@sec-iac). No claim is made for the parvovirus minute virus of mice (MVM), which has no lipid envelope for low pH to disrupt. No clearance of host cell protein is claimed for the step.

This report is paired with the plan PCP-006, under which the studies were run. Its results roll up into PCMR-001 with the reports of the other steps. @tbl-related lists the related documents.

```{python}
#| output: asis
#| label: tbl-related
#| tbl-cap: "Documents related to this report."
print(related_docs_md(DOC))
```

## Objectives

PCP-006 §2 set six objectives for the studies, and this report answers each of them.

1. To quantify the effects of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature, and of their interactions, on XMuLV clearance, aggregate, fragments and acidic variants (@sec-results).
2. To fit response-surface models that predict these outputs over the range studied, and to test each model against the adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 (@sec-rsm).
3. To determine, for each attribute that has a criterion at this step, the PAR of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature, and to establish whether the NOR of each lies within it (@sec-par).
4. To verify the platform worst cases of this step on which the criteria upstream of it rely (@sec-verif).
5. To assess the effect of A-Mab concentration on aggregate, acidic variants and XMuLV clearance one factor at a time, and to support its range against the criteria for aggregate and acidic variants (@sec-uni).
6. To provide the evidence for the classification of each parameter under SOP-4001, and for the contribution of the step to the control strategy in PCMR-001 (@sec-class, @sec-cs).

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The studies form the process design stage of the lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011]. They follow the enhanced approach of ICH Q8(R2) [@ichq8] and ICH Q11 [@ichq11], in which prior knowledge and risk assessment identify the parameters that may affect each attribute and designed experiments then measure and bound those effects. Criticality is treated as a continuum, as PCMP-001 §3 states it after ICH Q8(R2). The parameters were ranked under ICH Q9 in the risk assessment RA-001 before characterization began [@ichq9].

Viral safety follows ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a]. Each claimed step is studied in its own small-scale spiking model, a laboratory model of the step into which a known titre of the model virus is added, and the cumulative claim is built from the independent log reductions of low-pH inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration. The process model, the attribute framework and the decision logic for parameter classes come from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. The designs and their analysis follow standard response-surface methodology [@montgomery2017], with the Box-Cox transformation [@boxcox1964] and model selection by the small-sample information criterion AICc [@hurvich1989].

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The low-pH hold belongs to the Novacyte downstream platform and was used to manufacture three earlier humanized IgG1 antibodies, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. The process conditions of the step have remained essentially unchanged for those products and through the development of A-Mab [@amab2009]. That history supplies the platform claim for XMuLV clearance and the largest increases in aggregate, fragments and acidic variants the step has shown on the platform. The intermediate acceptance criteria of @sec-iac are built on those values, and @sec-verif checks them against the A-Mab data.

Low pH inactivates an enveloped virus by denaturing the glycoproteins of its envelope and by disrupting the envelope itself. The virus needs those glycoproteins to bind to a cell and to fuse with its membrane. Inactivation is commonly described by first-order kinetics, in which the log reduction grows with the hold time at a rate that rises as the pH falls and as the temperature rises. On that description a fall in pH was expected to raise the log reduction most steeply near the operating range, because the envelope glycoproteins denature much faster with each small fall in pH there. A longer hold and a warmer hold were each expected to raise the log reduction, and the effect of the hold time was expected to be larger at low pH. @sec-mech compares that description with the surface the data give.

The acid acts on the antibody as well as on the virus. At acid pH the second constant domain of the heavy chain is partially unfolded, which exposes hydrophobic surface. Molecules in that state associate, so aggregate forms for as long as the pool is held at low pH, and faster in a warmer pool, because both the unfolding and the association speed up with temperature. Aggregate formed in the hold is carried into cation exchange, the step that removes it. Time at low pH also adds acidic variants, through direct acid-catalysed hydrolysis of side-chain amides, and a small amount of acid-catalysed cleavage in the hinge region, which adds fragments. Over a hold of the length studied, both increases were expected to be small, the acidic variants against the level formed in the production bioreactor and the fragments against the level the load already carries.

The step was not expected to change the glycan attributes. Those are formed in the production bioreactor, and no downstream step changes them (PCMP-001 §3). The criteria also assume no change in host cell protein across the step.

## Quality attributes in scope

@tbl-cqa lists the attributes in scope, with their drug substance criteria and their criticality from the register of critical quality attributes (CQAs) in PCMP-001 §3. Criticality was assigned with Tool #1 of the A-Mab case study, as the product of impact and uncertainty [@amab2009]. XMuLV clearance was assigned very high criticality by rule, because a viral contamination would harm the patient directly whatever its score. Attributes of high or very high criticality are called critical.

```{python}
                      "Criticality": _cq["Criticality"], "Tool #1 score": [str(int(v)) for v in _cq["Tool #1"]]}),
        "Quality attributes in scope of this report, from the drug substance CQA register.", "tbl-cqa",

        notes=[("", "Tool #1, the score of impact multiplied by uncertainty (A-Mab case study). VH, very high. "
                    "H, high. L, low. VL, very low. Viral clearance is very high by rule, whatever its score."),
```

Aggregate and acidic variants are formed in the production bioreactor, and the register assigns fragments to harvest and clarification, where proteases released from lysed cells clip the antibody. The hold can add to each of those three, so each is measured at the output of this step and judged against an intermediate acceptance criterion (@sec-iac).

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

RA-001 assessed every parameter of the step before characterization began. Each parameter was ranked on its potential impact on the CQAs and on its potential to interact with other parameters, as ICH Q9 describes [@ichq9]. RA-001 gives the scores and the rationale for each assignment.

Inactivation pH, hold time and temperature were assigned to multivariate study. A lower pH, a longer hold and a warmer hold were each expected to raise the log reduction of XMuLV, and a longer or warmer hold to raise the aggregate that forms. The three were also expected to interact, because on the first-order description the log reduction is the product of a rate that depends on pH and temperature and the time over which that rate acts. A design that varies the three together was therefore needed to estimate the clearance and the aggregate at their combinations.

A-Mab concentration was assigned to univariate study. A higher antibody concentration raises the rate at which partially unfolded molecules meet, so aggregate was expected to form faster in a more concentrated pool. No effect of the antibody concentration on the inactivation of the virus was expected. The acid denatures the envelope of the virus, and the antibody neither shields the envelope nor takes part in that reaction. The concentration is also a property of the Protein A pool rather than a setting of the hold, so it was assessed one factor at a time.

# Materials and methods {#sec-methods}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The scale-down model holds the Protein A eluate in a temperature-controlled vessel at laboratory scale. The eluate is adjusted to the inactivation pH, held and neutralized in that vessel as in manufacture. The parameters of the step do not depend on scale, so inactivation pH, hold time, temperature and A-Mab concentration were set to the same values as in manufacture, and the additions of acid and base were scaled with the volume of the pool. The model was operated under SOP-2009 and qualified under SOP-1001.

The qualification study S-VI-SDM ran from `{python} win("S-VI-SDM")`, before the first characterization run. It compared `{python} int(off_agg["n_sd"])` runs of the scale-down model at set-point with `{python} int(off_agg["n_m"])` manufacturing-scale batches, for aggregate and acidic variants in the neutralized pool. @tbl-sdm-offsets gives the offset of each output, the scale-down mean minus the manufacturing mean, with its `{python} OFFCI` % confidence interval. Its last two columns give the qualification. The first of them shows whether the output meets its criterion at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high with the offset at the low end of its interval, at its estimate and at the high end.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sdm_offsets([UO], label="tbl-sdm-offsets").show()
```

Aggregate is `{python} fx(off_agg["offset"])` percentage points higher in the scale-down model and acidic variants `{python} fx(off_acid["offset"])` points higher, and neither interval excludes zero. Every result of these two outputs is translated to manufacturing scale by subtracting the offset of that output before it is compared with a criterion. The model is qualified for an output when the conclusion against its criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its interval (PCMP-001 §7.1). For aggregate that conclusion is the upper end of the single-run prediction interval of the selected model over the NOR against `{python} fx(crit_agg)` % HMW. For acidic variants, which have no adequate model, it is every measured result of the designs against `{python} fx(acid_lo, 1)` to `{python} fx(acid_hi, 1)` %. Both conclusions hold at all three values of the offset, so the model is qualified for aggregate and for acidic variants.

The qualification compared neither fragments nor XMuLV clearance at both scales, so the offset of each is unknown rather than zero. These two outputs are judged as the laboratory model gives them, with no translation to manufacturing scale. For fragments the representativeness of the model rests on the mechanism of the step, as PCP-006 §5.1 states it. Cleavage in the hinge region at low pH depends on pH, time and temperature, which the scale-down model sets to the manufacturing values, and not on the size of the vessel. The fragment results are far from their criterion, which bounds what the assumption can cost. The highest single result of the designs is `{python} fx(MEAS[FR].max())` %, which leaves `{python} fx(fr_margin)` points to the criterion of `{python} fx(crit_frag)` %. The assumption is stated as a limitation in @sec-discussion.

Virus cannot be introduced into the manufacturing process, so XMuLV clearance was measured in the spiking model of the step [@ichq5a]. PCP-006 §5.1 sets out the spiking model. It is the scale-down model, run on the same Protein A eluate and at the same inactivation pH, hold time and temperature. The XMuLV spike is added after the pool has been acidified and before the hold begins, at the volume ratio fixed in SOP-2009, which is small enough that the spike changes neither the pH nor the antibody concentration of the pool. The titre of the spiked pool is measured at the start of the hold and at the end. The virus load of a sample is its titre multiplied by the volume of the pool, and the log reduction factor (LRF) is the difference between the log~10~ load at the start and the log~10~ load at the end. Each run of a design is made twice, once spiked for the titres and once unspiked for the quality attributes. The inactivation rate depends on the pH, the temperature and the matrix of the pool, and not on its volume. The spiking runs use Protein A eluate produced at the set-points of the Protein A step, so the matrix is that of manufacture, and the runs of the designs held the A-Mab concentration at its set-point. The small-scale result therefore represents the manufacturing step at that concentration, provided the whole pool reaches the inactivation pH.

The centre points of each design are replicate runs at the design centre. They give the pure error against which lack of fit is tested (@sec-centre).

## Operation

The runs followed the operation of PCP-006 §5.2. Each run starts from Protein A eluate produced at the set-points of the Protein A step, which is characterized under PCR-005. The eluate is adjusted to the inactivation pH of the run and brought to its temperature, and the hold time is counted from the moment the inactivation pH is reached. At the end of the hold the pool is neutralized with base and filtered. Neutralization stops the inactivation and slows the reactions that the acid drives on the antibody. In both designs the A-Mab concentration was set to its set-point of `{python} sp_t["protein_conc"]`. The input pool was not tested, so that is the value set and not a measured result (PD-006-08). In the two concentration studies the concentration is set to each planned value before the pH is adjusted.

The acid and base solutions and the other inputs of the step are prepared to their platform specifications. They are controlled for identity and quality and were not characterized.

## Analytical methods

Each output was measured by a validated method under its own procedure. @tbl-sops lists the procedures and method validations this report cites. XMuLV titre was measured as the 50 % tissue culture infectious dose (TCID50) under AMV-3017, aggregate by SEC under AMV-3011, acidic variants by icIEF under AMV-3013 and fragments by nrCE-SDS under AMV-3020. Appendix D summarises the methods and their reportable units.

Those results are kept in the record and are used for no decision in this report. The retained samples of the response-surface design were tested by nrCE-SDS in the re-test study S-VI-RET, from `{python} win("S-VI-RET")`, and the fragment results of the designs are those `{python} n_rsm` results. Of the studies made during the re-analysis, `{python} join_and(FR_RE)` measured fragments by nrCE-SDS, and `{python} join_and(FR_RE_NOT)` measured none. The qualification study and the two concentration studies measured no fragments, and no fragment result is claimed for any of them. The effects on fragments therefore rest on the response-surface design (@sec-rsm), and the range of the A-Mab concentration is supported for aggregate and acidic variants but not for fragments (@sec-uni).

## Sampling plan

PCP-006 §5.4 sets out three samples from the spiked run and two from the unspiked run of each design run. The spiked run gives the input pool, the spiked load at the start of the hold and the spiked pool at the end, so the two titres of one LRF come from the same run. The unspiked run gives the input pool and the neutralized pool, sampled after neutralization and filtration, which is the level the step delivers to cation exchange. The record of both designs holds an LRF and a result for aggregate, acidic variants and fragments in the neutralized pool for every run, `{python} n_scr` screening runs and `{python} n_rsm` response-surface runs.

The input pool, to be sampled before acidification, was to give the level of aggregate, acidic variants and A-Mab concentration that the step starts from. It was not tested in either design, which is registered as the input-pool discrepancy PD-006-08 (@sec-record). The increase across the step that the verification of the platform worst cases needs is therefore taken against the aggregate level of the load in the process model at set-point, `{python} fx(FEED_AGG)` % HMW (@sec-verif).

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

Each factor is coded `{python} MINUS`1 at the low end of its range studied, +1 at the high end and 0 at the midpoint [@montgomery2017]. An effect is the change in the response over the coded range of the factor, which is twice its coefficient in coded units. A model term is significant when its p-value is below α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`, the level PCMP-001 §6.2 sets. About one term in twenty with no real effect is called significant at that level. A count of terms in this report counts the intercept as one of them.

The screening data were fitted by least squares with a model of main effects and two-factor interactions, which has `{python} W(len(SE[A]))` terms for three factors. The screening model identifies effects. Its centre points can detect curvature but cannot attribute it to a factor, so no prediction in this report comes from it. The response-surface model is the predictive model, and every prediction, every PAR, the design space and the verification of the platform worst cases come from it.

PCP-006 §5.5 prescribed the full quadratic model of each output, which has `{python} W(N_FULL_TERMS)` terms. This report selects the model of each output instead, as corrective action CA3 of `{python} INV2["id"]`, adopted on `{python} ca3_date`, requires for every report of the campaign. The change is registered as PD-006-04 (@sec-record). The selection has three steps.

1. *The scale.* The Box-Cox profile of the full quadratic estimates the exponent λ that would make the residuals of the model best behaved, with λ = 1 the raw scale and λ = 0 the log scale [@boxcox1964]. The log scale is used when the 95 % interval of λ contains 0 and excludes 1, which means the data support the log scale and reject the raw one.
2. *The model.* Among all `{python} N_SUB` submodels of the full quadratic that keep strong hierarchy, an interaction only with both its main effects and a square only with its main effect, the one with the lowest AICc is taken. AICc estimates how well a model would predict new runs and penalises every term it estimates, and its small-sample correction raises that penalty when the runs are few for the number of terms, as they are in a design of `{python} n_rsm` runs [@hurvich1989]. The residual variance counts as one of the estimated parameters.
3. *The check.* The selected model is judged against the four adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2. The first is a significant model F-test at α = `{python} g(ALPHA)`. The second is no significant lack of fit against pure error at α = `{python} g(LOFA)`. The third is a limit on overfitting, under which R² may exceed predicted R² by no more than `{python} fx(GAPMAX)`. The fourth, called the criterion on residuals and influential runs in this report, asks for residuals with no pattern against the predicted values or the run order and for no run dominating the fit. PCP-006 §7.1 tests it by two regressions, one of the absolute residuals on the predicted values and one of the residuals on the order of execution, each at α = `{python} g(RALPHA)`, and by the Cook's distance of each run. A run whose Cook's distance exceeds `{python} g(COOKF)`/n, which is `{python} fx(cook_lim)` for `{python} n_rsm` runs, is examined by deleting it, selecting the model again on the remaining runs and judging the output over the NOR again. The model fails the criterion where a run exceeds the `{python} F_Q` % quantile of the F distribution with the degrees of freedom of the model, which is a much larger distance. Predicted R² comes from the prediction error sum of squares, in which each run is predicted by the model fitted without it [@montgomery2017]. An output with no adequate model sets no range and is judged on its measured results.

A model that reproduces its results exactly is never adequate. With no residual there is no pure error for the lack-of-fit test and no residual mean square for the model F-test, so the criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 cannot be applied, and the prediction interval of such a model has zero width. The acidic variants of this step are such an output (@sec-rsm).

Aggregate, fragments and acidic variants must meet their criteria in every batch, and a response-surface model predicts the mean response. Each of them is therefore judged through the `{python} PI` % prediction interval of a single run, which stands for a single batch, at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the three factors, with the offset of the scale-down model applied. That interval is two-sided, so its upper end is a one-sided `{python} fx(100 - (100 - PI) / 2, 1)` % limit. XMuLV clearance is judged on the mean predicted LRF at the least favourable of those combinations. Viral clearance is validated at worst-case conditions, so the claim has to hold there, and this report gives that reason nowhere else. The prediction interval of a single run of the log reduction is reported beside it for information.

PCMP-001 §6.4 defines two PAR analyses per attribute and factor. The second, which PCMP-001 calls the NOR-propagated PAR, is the range of the factor over which the attribute meets its criterion while the other two factors vary within their NORs. For a quality attribute it draws `{python} f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}"` operating points of the other two factors at each of `{python} D.PAR_GRID` grid points, each factor from a normal distribution centred on its set-point whose standard deviation is one sixth of the width of its NOR, clipped to the range studied, and compares the central 95 % of the simulated batches with the criterion. For XMuLV clearance it draws nothing. At each grid point the other two factors take every combination of their NOR low, set-point and NOR high, and the lowest mean prediction is compared with the claim. The verification of the platform worst cases uses the one-sided `{python} VB` % prediction bound of a single batch (@sec-verif). Commercial-scale capability comes from the integrated model of the train, which runs `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` simulated batches through every step (@sec-capability).

One analysis of this report is in no plan. PCP-006 sets no rule for models that fit almost as well as the selected one. Where another model lies within 2 AICc units of the selected one, that model was fitted and its conclusions compared with those of the selected model, which decides. The comparison is registered within PD-006-04 (@sec-near).
