The ranges studied were set in RA-001 and PCP-006 §6.1. Inactivation pH was studied from `{python} g(RNG["ph"][0])` to `{python} g(RNG["ph"][1])`, wider than the NOR on both sides, which shows how the step behaves near and beyond the edges of routine operation. Hold time was studied from `{python} g(RNG["hold_time"][0])` to `{python} g(RNG["hold_time"][1])` min. Its lower end was the shortest hold the NOR of PCP-006 allowed, and it is the least favourable condition for XMuLV clearance. Its upper end is `{python} fx(RNG["hold_time"][1] / NORc["hold_time"][1], 1)` times the longest hold of that NOR and shows how aggregate and fragments grow in a long hold. Temperature was studied from `{python} g(RNG["temperature"][0])` to `{python} g(RNG["temperature"][1])` °C, the range a manufacturing suite delivers. The A-Mab concentration of the Protein A pool varies from `{python} g(RNG["protein_conc"][0])` to `{python} g(RNG["protein_conc"][1])` g/L, and its NOR equals that range.

The centre of each design is the midpoint of the ranges studied, at `{python} wu("ph", g(CENTRE["ph"]))`, `{python} wu("hold_time", g(CENTRE["hold_time"]))` and `{python} wu("temperature", g(CENTRE["temperature"]))`. It is the set-point of none of the three factors, because the ranges are not symmetrical about the set-points. The centre points therefore estimate pure error at the design centre, and each model predicts the outputs at the set-point from the fitted surface rather than measuring them there.

## Screening design

The screening design S-VI-SCR was a two-level full factorial design in inactivation pH, hold time and temperature with `{python} c_scr` centre points, `{python} n_scr` runs in all, executed in random order from `{python} win("S-VI-SCR")`. Every combination of the low and high ends of the three ranges was run, so the design estimates all three main effects and all three two-factor interactions without aliasing. Its purpose was to identify which factors and interactions act on each output. The design matrix and the results are in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface design S-VI-RSM was a face-centred central composite design in the same three factors, with `{python} n_fac_rsm` factorial runs, `{python} n_ax` axial runs and `{python} c_rsm` centre points, `{python} n_rsm` runs in all, executed in random order from `{python} win("S-VI-RSM")` [@montgomery2017]. The axial runs lie at the centres of the faces of the design cube, at the ends of each range studied, so every run stayed inside the range studied. Together with the centre points they allow a squared term to be estimated for each factor. PCP-006 §6.2 carried every factor with a detected effect into this design, and the screening had detected an effect of each of the three on XMuLV clearance (@sec-screening). Every output of the neutralized pool was measured on every run. The input pool was not tested (PD-006-08). The design matrix and the results are in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

A-Mab concentration was assessed one factor at a time in study S-VI-UNI, from `{python} win("S-VI-UNI")`. The low-pH hold was run at `{python} g(RNG["protein_conc"][0])` and `{python} g(RNG["protein_conc"][1])` g/L in duplicate, with the other three parameters at their set-points as characterized, and the set-point runs of the qualification study served as the reference at set-point. PCP-006 §6.4 required aggregate, acidic variants and the log reduction of XMuLV on every run. The study measured aggregate and acidic variants only, which is registered as PD-006-07, the clearance the concentration study did not measure (@sec-record). The clearance across the concentration range was measured in the confirmation study S-VI-UNI2, from `{python} win("S-VI-UNI2")`, registered as PD-006-06, the clearance at the two ends of the concentration range. A study of one factor at a time cannot show whether the effect of the concentration depends on the other parameters, and the designs, which held the concentration at its set-point, carry no information on a concentration effect.

`{python} W(len(RE_STUDIES)).capitalize()` studies beyond the plan were made during the Version 2.0 re-analysis and are reported here. @tbl-chronology gives the execution window of every study of the step and of the cation exchange verification runs, in the order in which they started.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_lab = {"S-VI-SDM": "Scale-down model qualification", "S-VI-SCR": "Screening design",
        "S-VI-RSM": "Response-surface design", "S-VI-UNI": "A-Mab concentration, aggregate and acidic variants",
        "S-VI-RET": "Re-test of retained samples by nrCE-SDS",
        "S-VI-UNI2": "XMuLV clearance at both ends of the A-Mab concentration range",
        "S-VI-HLD": "Hold of the neutralized pool", "S-VI-OFAT": "Quality attributes at the new pH set-point",
        "S-CEX-VER": "Cation exchange runs on material at the new pH set-point",
        "S-VI-WC": "Confirmation runs at the low end of the pH PAR, hold time and temperature at their NOR highs"}
_ch = pd.concat([CHR.loc[CHAR_STUDIES].assign(Phase="Characterization"),
                 CHR.loc[RE_STUDIES].assign(Phase="Version 2.0 re-analysis")]).reset_index()
_ch = _ch.sort_values(["Phase", "start", "end"], kind="stable")
_ch = _ch.assign(**{"Study type": _ch["id"].map(_lab)}).rename(columns={"id": "Study", "start": "Start", "end": "End"})
T.frame(_ch[["Phase", "Study", "Study type", "Start", "End"]],
        "Execution window of every study reported here.", "tbl-chronology", merge=["Phase"],
        align=["P{2.8cm}", "l", "P{6.4cm}", "l", "l"],
        notes=[("", "Start, the date of the first run or test of a study. End, the date of the last. "
                    "The cation exchange verification runs are a study of the cation exchange scale-down "
                    "model on material from this step.")]).show()
```

Every characterization study closed before Version 1.0 of this report was approved on `{python} rev1_date(DOC)`, and the first of them started after PCP-006 Version 1.0 was approved on `{python} PLAN_APPROVAL["PCP-006"]`. The `{python} W(len(RE_STUDIES))` studies of the re-analysis ran from `{python} re_start` to `{python} re_end`, after `{python} INV["id"]` closed on `{python} INV["closed"]`. The set-points and NORs of this revision were decided on the results of the designs. The hold at the new pH set-point, S-VI-OFAT, and the cation exchange verification runs tested that set-point after it had been decided, and the confirmation runs were made after the hold-time NOR had been revised (@sec-nor).

# Results {#sec-results}

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility {#sec-centre}

@tbl-centre gives the mean, the standard deviation and the coefficient of variation of each response over the centre points of both designs. These replicates are the pure-error basis of the lack-of-fit tests in @sec-rsm.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_cc = pd.concat([D.center_cv_df(UO, "screening").assign(Design="Screening"),
                 D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm").assign(Design="Response surface")])
T.frame(_cc[["Design", "Response", "n", "Mean", "SD", "%CV"]].assign(
            Mean=lambda d: [T.num(v) for v in d["Mean"]], SD=lambda d: [f"{v:.3g}" for v in d["SD"]],
            **{"%CV": lambda d: [f"{v:.2f}" for v in d["%CV"]]}),
        "Centre-point reproducibility of each response in both designs.", "tbl-centre",
        merge=["Design"], align=["P{3.4cm}", "P{4.2cm}", "c", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "n, the number of centre-point runs. SD, standard deviation of the replicates. "
                    "%CV, the standard deviation as a percentage of the mean. Aggregate and acidic "
                    "variants in percent, XMuLV log reduction in log10.")]).show()
```

The XMuLV log reduction is the least precise response. Its coefficient of variation is `{python} fx(CVR.loc[LAB[X], "%CV"], 1)` % over the `{python} c_rsm` centre points of the response-surface design, which is a standard deviation of `{python} fx(CVR.loc[LAB[X], "SD"])` log~10~. An infectivity titre carries the variability of a cell-based assay (PCP-006 §12), and an LRF is the difference of two log~10~ virus loads, so it carries that variability twice. Aggregate reproduces to `{python} fx(CVR.loc[LAB[A], "%CV"], 1)` %, a standard deviation of `{python} fx(CVR.loc[LAB[A], "SD"], 3)` percentage points. Fragments, measured by nrCE-SDS on the retained samples of the response-surface design, reproduce to a standard deviation of `{python} fx(fr_c_sd, 3)` points about a mean of `{python} fx(fr_c_mean)` % over those `{python} c_rsm` runs.

The acidic variants gave the same result at every centre point of both designs, so their coefficient of variation is zero. Across both designs and the first concentration study, `{python} n_acid_flat` results in all, the attribute took one value per hold time and nothing else, `{python} fx(ACID_H[RNG["hold_time"][0]], 1)` % at `{python} g(RNG["hold_time"][0])` min, `{python} fx(ACID_H[acid_u1_hold], 1)` % at `{python} g(acid_u1_hold)` min in the concentration study, `{python} fx(ACID_H[CENTRE["hold_time"]], 1)` % at `{python} g(CENTRE["hold_time"])` min and `{python} fx(ACID_H[RNG["hold_time"][1]], 1)` % at `{python} g(RNG["hold_time"][1])` min. There is no scatter about those values and no dependence on pH or temperature. The same method gave a repeatability of `{python} fx(OF.loc[AC, "method_sd"])` percentage points on the same attribute in S-VI-OFAT (@sec-ofat), and the four runs of the second concentration study gave four different values, so the record holds scatter on this attribute elsewhere and none in the designs. The record gives no reason for that. The consequence for the analysis is that no adequacy test can be applied to the model of this output (@sec-rsm).

The centre-point mean of the XMuLV log reduction was `{python} fx(d_centre)` log~10~ higher in the screening design than in the response-surface design, which is `{python} fx(d_centre / sd_pe_x, 1)` times the pure-error standard deviation of `{python} fx(sd_pe_x)` log~10~ at the design centre. @sec-screening compares the two designs at the settings they share.

## Screening: factor effects {#sec-screening}

@tbl-screen-fit gives the fit of the screening model of each response, and @tbl-screen-eff the effect estimates. An effect is the change in the response from the low to the high end of the range studied.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_sf = D.fit_summary_df(UO, "screening")
_rows = []
for _, r_ in _sf.iterrows():
    _ex = r_["Response"] == LAB[AC]
    _rows.append({"Response": r_["Response"], "Runs": str(int(r_["N"])), "R²": f"{r_['R²']:.3f}",
                  "Adj. R²": f"{r_['Adj. R²']:.3f}", "Pred. R²": f"{r_['Pred. R²']:.3f}",
                  "F": "n.a." if _ex else f"{r_['F']:.1f}", "p-value": "n.a." if _ex else pfmt(r_["p-value"]),
                  "RMSE": "n.a." if _ex else s3(r_["RMSE"])})
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_rows), "Screening models of the low-pH viral inactivation step.", "tbl-screen-fit",
        align=["P{3.6cm}", "c", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "Main effects and two-factor interactions in coded units. RMSE, residual standard "
                    "deviation, in the unit of the response. n.a., not applicable: the model reproduces "
                    "the acidic variant results exactly, so it has no residual and no test.")]).show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
_se = pd.concat([D.screening_effects_df(UO, r).assign(Response=LAB[r]) for r in (A, X)])
_se = _se[["Response", "Term", "Effect", "Coef.", "Std. err.", "p-value", "Sig."]]
T.frame(_se.assign(Effect=lambda d: [fx(v, 3) for v in d["Effect"]],
                   **{"Coef.": lambda d: [fx(v, 3) for v in d["Coef."]],
                      "Std. err.": lambda d: [f"{v:.4f}" for v in d["Std. err."]],
                      "p-value": lambda d: [pfmt(v) for v in d["p-value"]]}),
        "Screening effects on aggregate and on XMuLV log reduction, largest first.", "tbl-screen-eff",
        merge=["Response"], align=["P{3.6cm}", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "l"],
        notes=[("", "Effect, the change in the response over the coded range of the factor, which is "
                    "twice the coefficient. Terms: A, inactivation pH. B, hold time. C, temperature. "
                    "AB, AC and BC are the two-factor interactions."),
               ("", "Sig., significance of the term. *, p < 0.05. **, p < 0.01. ***, p < 0.001.")]).show()
```

Each of the three factors changed the XMuLV log reduction. A fall in pH across the range studied raised it by `{python} fx(abs(SE[X].loc["A", "Effect"]))` log~10~ (`{python} pv(SE[X].loc["A", "p-value"])`), a longer hold by `{python} fx(SE[X].loc["B", "Effect"])` log~10~ (`{python} pv(SE[X].loc["B", "p-value"])`) and a warmer hold by `{python} fx(SE[X].loc["C", "Effect"])` log~10~ (`{python} pv(SE[X].loc["C", "p-value"])`). No interaction reached significance. All three factors were therefore carried into the response-surface design, as PCP-006 §6.2 planned for a factor with a detected effect.

Aggregate responded to hold time and temperature. A longer hold raised it by `{python} fx(SE[A].loc["B", "Effect"], 3)` percentage points (`{python} pv(SE[A].loc["B", "p-value"])`) and a warmer hold by `{python} fx(SE[A].loc["C", "Effect"], 3)` points (`{python} pv(SE[A].loc["C", "p-value"])`). The effect of pH was `{python} fx(SE[A].loc["A", "Effect"], 3)` points and did not reach significance (`{python} pv(SE[A].loc["A", "p-value"])`), and no interaction did either. The acidic variants gave an effect of hold time alone, of `{python} fx(SE_AC.loc["B", "Effect"], 1)` percentage points over the range studied, and no residual scatter, so the fit statistics of that model carry no information (@tbl-screen-fit).

Fragments were measured by SEC in the screening design, and those results are biased in this matrix (@sec-methods). They are reported in Appendix A for completeness and are used for no decision, so the effects on fragments in this report rest on the `{python} n_rsm` nrCE-SDS results of the response-surface design alone (@sec-rsm).

The screening and the response-surface design shared their eight corner settings, and the XMuLV log reduction differed between them. At the four corners at pH `{python} g(RNG["ph"][0])` the screening runs read `{python} fx(d_low_ph)` log~10~ higher on average, and at the four corners at pH `{python} g(RNG["ph"][1])` the two designs agreed to `{python} fx(abs(d_high_ph))` log~10~, which is less than the pure-error standard deviation. The pH effect was therefore larger in the screening design than in the response-surface design, `{python} fx(abs(_cmp["ph"]["scr"]))` against `{python} fx(abs(_cmp["ph"]["rsm"]))` log~10~, and the difference is significant when the two estimates are compared against their standard errors (`{python} pv(_cmp["ph"]["p"])`). For hold time and temperature no difference between the designs was detected (`{python} pv(_cmp["hold_time"]["p"])` and `{python} pv(_cmp["temperature"]["p"])`). The record holds the log reduction of each run and no titre, so whether an output titre at pH `{python} g(RNG["ph"][0])`, where the clearance is largest, reached the lowest titre the assay can report cannot be checked from it. Cytotoxicity of the assay at low dilution raises that lowest titre, and a higher output titre makes a computed log reduction smaller, so DEV-006-02 is one possible contributor to the difference. The record names no cause. The response-surface model is the predictive model of this report, and it gives the smaller pH effect, so the design space and the ranges rest on the smaller estimate.

## Response-surface models {#sec-rsm}

@tbl-reeval-viral-inactivation gives, for each output with a criterion, the fit of the full quadratic model that PCP-006 §5.5 planned, on the `{python} n_rsm` planned runs, and in its last column the terms of the model the output ends up with under the selection of @sec-stats. The design has one block, so no selected model carries a block term.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.model_reevaluation(UO, label="tbl-reeval-viral-inactivation").show()
```

The Box-Cox profile chose the raw scale for every output that has one. The estimates of the exponent λ are `{python} fx(BC[A]["lambda"])` for aggregate, `{python} fx(BC[X]["lambda"])` for the XMuLV log reduction and `{python} fx(BC[FR]["lambda"])` for fragments, and each 95 % interval contains the raw scale as well as the log scale. The data therefore do not reject the raw scale, and every coefficient and prediction below is in the unit of its attribute. The acidic variants have no Box-Cox interval, because every exponent fits their results exactly.

The selected model of aggregate carries `{python} terms_text(FIT[A]["names"])`. @tbl-coef-agg gives its coefficients and @tbl-anova-agg the partition of its sums of squares.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_cd = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, A)
T.frame(pd.DataFrame({"Term": _cd["Term"], "Coefficient": [s3(v) for v in _cd["Coef."]],
                       "Std. err.": [s3(v) for v in _cd["Std. err."]], "t": [s3(v) for v in _cd["t"]],
                       "p-value": [pfmt(v) for v in _cd["p-value"]]}),
        "Coefficients of the selected model of aggregate (% HMW).", "tbl-coef-agg", align=["l", "r", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "Coded units, so a coefficient is half the change over the range studied. Terms: "
                    "A, inactivation pH. B, hold time. C, temperature.")]).show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
_an = D.anova_lof_df(UO, A)
_e = lambda v, f: "" if pd.isna(v) else f(v)
T.frame(pd.DataFrame({"Source": [s.strip() for s in _an["Source"]],
                       "Sum of squares": [_e(v, s3) for v in _an["Sum sq."]],
                       "df": [str(int(v)) for v in _an["df"]],
                       "Mean square": [_e(v, s3) for v in _an["Mean sq."]],
                       "F": [_e(v, lambda x: f"{x:.2f}") for v in _an["F"]],
                       "p-value": [_e(v, pfmt) for v in _an["p-value"]]}),
        "Model, lack-of-fit and pure-error partition of the selected model of aggregate.", "tbl-anova-agg", align=["l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "Lack of fit and pure error partition the residual. Pure error comes from the "
                    "centre points.")]).show()
```

A hold of the full range studied raises aggregate by `{python} fx(EFA["hold_time"], 3)` percentage points (`{python} pv(PA["hold_time"])`) and the full temperature range by `{python} fx(EFA["temperature"], 3)` points (`{python} pv(PA["temperature"])`). The model explains R² = `{python} fx(FIT[A]["R2"], 3)` of the variation, with an adjusted R² of `{python} fx(FIT[A]["adjR2"], 3)`, and predicts left-out runs at predicted R² = `{python} fx(FIT[A]["predR2"], 3)`, a difference of `{python} fx(FIT[A]["gap"], 3)` against the limit of `{python} fx(GAPMAX)`. The model F-test is significant (`{python} pv(FIT[A]["p"])`) and lack of fit against the pure error of the centre points is not (`{python} pv(FIT[A]["p_lof"])`). The selection dropped the pH term, so every prediction of aggregate in this report comes from a model in which pH does not appear. On the full quadratic model of the planned runs the pH effect lies between `{python} fx(agg_ph_lo, 3)` and `{python} fx(agg_ph_hi, 3)` percentage points over the whole range studied, so these data bound a linear effect of pH on aggregate within about `{python} fx(max(abs(agg_ph_lo), abs(agg_ph_hi)), 2)` points. That bound is the size of the effect the dropped term could carry.

The selected model of the XMuLV log reduction carries `{python} terms_text(FIT[X]["names"])`. @tbl-coef-xmulv gives its coefficients and @tbl-anova-xmulv its partition.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_cd = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, X)
T.frame(pd.DataFrame({"Term": _cd["Term"], "Coefficient": [s3(v) for v in _cd["Coef."]],
                       "Std. err.": [s3(v) for v in _cd["Std. err."]], "t": [s3(v) for v in _cd["t"]],
                       "p-value": [pfmt(v) for v in _cd["p-value"]]}),
        "Coefficients of the selected model of the XMuLV log reduction (log10).", "tbl-coef-xmulv", align=["l", "r", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "Coded units, so a coefficient is half the change over the range studied. Terms: "
                    "A, inactivation pH. B, hold time. C, temperature.")]).show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
_an = D.anova_lof_df(UO, X)
_e = lambda v, f: "" if pd.isna(v) else f(v)
T.frame(pd.DataFrame({"Source": [s.strip() for s in _an["Source"]],
                       "Sum of squares": [_e(v, s3) for v in _an["Sum sq."]],
                       "df": [str(int(v)) for v in _an["df"]],
                       "Mean square": [_e(v, s3) for v in _an["Mean sq."]],
                       "F": [_e(v, lambda x: f"{x:.2f}") for v in _an["F"]],
                       "p-value": [_e(v, pfmt) for v in _an["p-value"]]}),
        "Model, lack-of-fit and pure-error partition of the selected model of the XMuLV log reduction.", "tbl-anova-xmulv", align=["l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "Lack of fit and pure error partition the residual. Pure error comes from the "
                    "centre points.")]).show()
```

A rise in pH across the range studied lowers the log reduction by `{python} fx(abs(EFX["ph"]))` log~10~ (`{python} pv(PX["ph"])`), a hold of the full range studied raises it by `{python} fx(EFX["hold_time"])` log~10~ (`{python} pv(PX["hold_time"])`) and the full temperature range by `{python} fx(EFX["temperature"])` log~10~ (`{python} pv(PX["temperature"])`). The model explains R² = `{python} fx(FIT[X]["R2"], 3)`, with an adjusted R² of `{python} fx(FIT[X]["adjR2"], 3)` and a predicted R² of `{python} fx(FIT[X]["predR2"], 3)`, a difference of `{python} fx(FIT[X]["gap"], 3)` between R² and predicted R², again within the limit. The model F-test is significant (`{python} pv(FIT[X]["p"])`) and lack of fit is not (`{python} pv(FIT[X]["p_lof"])`). Its residual standard deviation is `{python} fx(FIT[X]["rmse"])` log~10~, close to the pure-error standard deviation of the centre points, `{python} fx(sd_pe_x)` log~10~, so the model leaves no more scatter than replicate runs at the same settings show. No interaction entered the model, and @sec-mech bounds the interaction of pH with hold time on the full quadratic model the plan prescribed.

Acidic variants and fragments have no adequate model. For the acidic variants the full quadratic reproduces every result exactly, as @sec-centre shows, and the criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 cannot be applied to such a fit (@sec-stats). The model that the selection returns carries `{python} terms_text(FIT[AC]["names"])` and is not adequate, so it sets no range and the attribute is judged on its measured results. Those results depend on hold time alone (@sec-mech).

For fragments the selected model carries `{python} terms_text(FIT[FR]["names"])`. It is significant (`{python} pv(FIT[FR]["p"])`) and shows no lack of fit (`{python} pv(FIT[FR]["p_lof"])`), but R² = `{python} fx(FIT[FR]["R2"], 3)` (adjusted R² `{python} fx(FIT[FR]["adjR2"], 3)`) falls to predicted R² = `{python} fx(FIT[FR]["predR2"], 3)`, a difference of `{python} fx(FIT[FR]["gap"], 3)` against the limit of `{python} fx(GAPMAX)`. The model therefore has more terms than these data support, and it sets no range. It does meet the criterion on residuals and influential runs. Neither residual regression is significant (`{python} pv(RI[FR]["p_spread"])` and `{python} pv(RI[FR]["p_order"])`), and no run reaches the F limit, although runs `{python} join_and(RI[FR]["over"])` carry a Cook's distance above the cut-off for examination. Fragments are judged on the `{python} len(MEAS[FR])` nrCE-SDS results of the response-surface design, which run from `{python} fx(MEAS[FR].min())` to `{python} fx(MEAS[FR].max())` %. At the rate S-VI-OFAT measured (@sec-ofat) the hold adds about `{python} fx(fr_rise_range)` points over the whole hold-time range studied, which is `{python} fx(fr_ratio, 1)` times the repeatability of nrCE-SDS, `{python} fx(fr_sd)` points, and leaves `{python} fx(fr_margin)` points to the criterion.


Both selected models meet the criterion on residuals and influential runs, the fourth of PCMP-001 §7.2. Neither regression of that test is significant for either model. For aggregate the absolute residuals do not grow with the predicted value (`{python} pv(RI[A]["p_spread"])`) and the residuals do not drift with the order of execution (`{python} pv(RI[A]["p_order"])`), and the fitted drift over the `{python} n_rsm` runs is `{python} fx(TREND[A]["order"], 3)` percentage points, against a margin of `{python} fx(crit_agg - UPL_A)` points between the highest single-batch prediction over the NOR and the criterion. For the XMuLV log reduction the two p-values are `{python} pv(RI[X]["p_spread"])` and `{python} pv(RI[X]["p_order"])`, and the fitted drift is `{python} fx(TREND[X]["order"])` log~10~ against a margin of `{python} fx(WC_X["predicted"] - claim)` log~10~ between the lowest mean prediction over the NOR and the claim. That drift is `{python} fx(100 * TREND[X]["order"] / (WC_X["predicted"] - claim), 0)` % of the margin, and it is not significant.

No run dominates either fit. The criterion fails where a run's Cook's distance exceeds the `{python} F_Q` % quantile of the F distribution with the degrees of freedom of the model, which is `{python} fx(RI[A]["f_limit"])` for the aggregate model and `{python} fx(RI[X]["f_limit"])` for the XMuLV model. The largest Cook's distance is `{python} fx(RI[A]["cook_max"])` at run `{python} RI[A]["cook_run"]` for aggregate and `{python} fx(RI[X]["cook_max"])` at run `{python} RI[X]["cook_run"]` for the XMuLV log reduction, so neither model fails. Both lie above the cut-off of `{python} fx(cook_lim)` at which PCP-006 §7.1 calls for an examination. `{python} W(len(RI[A]["over"])).capitalize()` runs of the aggregate model are above that cut-off, runs `{python} join_and(RI[A]["over"])`, and `{python} W(len(RI[X]["over"]))` of the XMuLV model, runs `{python} join_and(RI[X]["over"])`. @sec-influence gives the examination of each.

### Models near the selected one {#sec-near}

For three outputs another model lies within 2 AICc units of the selected one. @tbl-near lists those models with their adequacy and the judgement each gives. The comparison is registered within PD-006-04.

```{python}

for r in (A, X, FR):
    for n_ in NEAR[r]:
```

For aggregate the three models within 2 units share hold time and temperature and differ in a squared temperature term and a hold time by temperature interaction. All three give an upper single-batch limit within `{python} fx(max(n_["value"] for n_ in NEAR[A]) - min(n_["value"] for n_ in NEAR[A]), 3)` percentage points of one another, and all three meet the criterion across the NOR. The model with the interaction does not meet all four adequacy criteria, because run `{python} near_a_run` carries a Cook's distance above the F limit in it, and the selected model decides in any case. For the XMuLV log reduction the three models share pH and hold time, two of them keep temperature and one adds a squared pH term. All three meet the four criteria. The lowest mean prediction over the NOR ranges from `{python} fx(min(n_["value"] for n_ in NEAR[X]))` to `{python} fx(max(n_["value"] for n_ in NEAR[X]))` log~10~ among them, and the claim of `{python} fx(claim)` log~10~ is met under each. For fragments the four models within 2 units disagree about the form of the surface. Three of them carry a squared pH term and exceed the limit on overfitting, and one of those three also fails the criterion on residuals and influential runs. The fourth carries hold time alone and meets all four criteria, and it lies `{python} fx(NEAR[FR][2]["d_aicc"])` AICc units above the selected model. The selected model decides, so fragments set no range, and their predicted levels are not carried into any conclusion of this report.

Four conclusions of this report hold under every deletion. The NOR in force stays inside the PAR of each of the three factors, the claim is met across the NOR in force, the pH NOR still has to move to meet it, and inactivation pH stays a critical process parameter, hold time and temperature well-controlled critical process parameters and A-Mab concentration a general process parameter. For aggregate the model selected after a deletion keeps hold time and temperature in every case and adds a third term in two of the three. Temperature raises aggregate by `{python} fx(agg_temp_lo, 3)` to `{python} fx(agg_temp_hi, 3)` percentage points over the range studied in those models, against `{python} fx(EFA["temperature"], 3)` points on all runs, and the effect is significant in every one of them (`{python} pv(agg_temp_p_max)` at its weakest). The upper single-batch limit over the NOR moves by at most `{python} fx(max(abs(i_["value"] - UPL_A) for i_ in INF[A]), 3)` percentage points, the criterion is met in every case, and the highest single-batch limit anywhere in the region studied is `{python} fx(inf_agg_upper)` %, still below `{python} fx(crit_agg)` %. The one-sided `{python} VB` % prediction bound of the aggregate increase within the NOR as characterized, which replaced the platform worst case upstream of this step, is at most `{python} fx(max(i_["bound"] for i_ in INF[A]))` percentage points after any one deletion, against `{python} fx(v_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"])` on all runs and a platform value of `{python} fx(v_agg["assumed"])`, so it stays below the platform value in every case (@sec-verif).

Two results of the XMuLV model do depend on run `{python} INF5["run"]`. With that run deleted the temperature term leaves the model, so the temperature effect on the log reduction of `{python} fx(EFX["temperature"])` log~10~ (`{python} pv(PX["temperature"])`) rests on it. The PAR of each factor widens when the run is deleted. The pH PAR runs to pH `{python} g(INF5["par"]["ph"][1])` instead of pH `{python} g(PE["ph"][1])`, the hold-time PAR begins at `{python} g(INF5["par"]["hold_time"][0])` min instead of `{python} g(PE["hold_time"][0])` min, and the temperature PAR covers the whole range studied. The deletion of run `{python} INF4["run"]` keeps all three terms and moves the PARs little. Under every model the ranges reported in @sec-par are the narrowest of the three, so the NOR in force lies inside the PAR under each of them, and the lowest mean prediction over the NOR in force is `{python} fx(INF[X][0]["value"])` and `{python} fx(INF[X][1]["value"])` log~10~, above the claim in both cases. Over the NOR as characterized the claim fails under both deleted models as it does under the selected model, at `{python} fx(INF[X][0]["value_char"])` and `{python} fx(INF[X][1]["value_char"])` log~10~ against `{python} fx(WC_Xc["predicted"])` log~10~, so the decision to move the NOR does not rest on one run.

## Mechanistic interpretation {#sec-mech}

@fig-xmulv shows the predicted XMuLV log reduction over pH and hold time at the two ends of the temperature NOR in force.

```{python}
#| label: fig-xmulv
#| fig-cap: "Predicted XMuLV log reduction over inactivation pH and hold time, at the two ends of the temperature NOR in force. The claim of the step is drawn as a white contour, the NOR in force as a grey box. Lighter shading is a larger log reduction."
_gp = np.linspace(RNG["ph"][0], RNG["ph"][1], 60)
_gt = np.linspace(RNG["hold_time"][0], RNG["hold_time"][1], 60)
_PP, _TT = np.meshgrid(_gp, _gt)
_fig, _ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.9), sharey=True)
for _a, _tmp in zip(_ax, NOR["temperature"]):
    _Z = D.predict(UO, X, natural={"ph": _PP.ravel(), "hold_time": _TT.ravel(),
                                   "temperature": np.full(_PP.size, _tmp)}).reshape(_PP.shape)
    _cs = _a.contourf(_PP, _TT, _Z, levels=12, cmap="viridis")
    _cl = _a.contour(_PP, _TT, _Z, levels=[claim], colors="white", linewidths=1.6)
    _a.clabel(_cl, fmt={claim: f"{claim:g} log10"}, fontsize=7)
    _fig.colorbar(_cs, ax=_a, shrink=0.85)
    _a.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((NOR["ph"][0], NOR["hold_time"][0]), NOR["ph"][1] - NOR["ph"][0],
                               NOR["hold_time"][1] - NOR["hold_time"][0], fill=False, color="0.25", lw=1.2))
    _a.annotate("NOR", (NOR["ph"][1], NOR["hold_time"][1]), xytext=(4, 4), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=7)
    _a.set_title(f"{NAME['temperature']} {g(_tmp)} {UNIT['temperature']}", fontsize=10)
    _a.set_xlabel(f"{NAME['ph']} ({UNIT['ph']})")
_ax[0].set_ylabel(f"{NAME['hold_time']} ({UNIT['hold_time']})")
_fig.suptitle("Mean predicted XMuLV log reduction (log10)", fontsize=11)
_fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.94])
plt.show()
```

The log reduction falls as the pH rises and grows as the hold lengthens, and the contour of the claim runs from the bottom left of each panel to the top right. The surface the data give is a plane in the three factors. It carries no interaction of pH with hold time, so the hold time that restores the claim after a rise in pH is the same at every pH within the range studied, and it carries no curvature, so the log reduction grows at a constant rate with the hold time. The first-order description of @sec-prior predicts the opposite on both counts. A log reduction of k(pH, T) multiplied by the hold time rises faster with time the lower the pH, which is an interaction, and these data show none. On the full quadratic model of the planned runs that interaction lies between `{python} fx(x_ab_lo)` and `{python} fx(x_ab_hi)` log~10~ over the corners of the range studied (`{python} pv(x_ab_p)`), so `{python} n_rsm` runs bound it rather than resolve it. The first-order description does not explain the plane, and the surface reported here is what the data give over the range studied. The three factors trade against one another on it. A rise of `{python} fx(nor_half_ph)` pH units, the half-width of the pH NOR, lowers the log reduction by `{python} fx(nor_half_ph * abs(EFX["ph"]) / (RNG["ph"][1] - RNG["ph"][0]))` log~10~, which a hold longer by `{python} fx(nor_half_ph * (abs(EFX["ph"]) / (RNG["ph"][1] - RNG["ph"][0])) / (EFX["hold_time"] / (RNG["hold_time"][1] - RNG["hold_time"][0])), 0)` min or warmer by `{python} fx(nor_half_ph * (abs(EFX["ph"]) / (RNG["ph"][1] - RNG["ph"][0])) / (EFX["temperature"] / (RNG["temperature"][1] - RNG["temperature"][0])), 1)` °C offsets. A pool at manufacturing scale reaches its pH by acid addition and mixing, and a pH above the one intended lowers the log reduction. That is why the claim is most exposed to the inactivation pH (@sec-class).

Aggregate grows with the hold time and with the temperature, which is the direction the association of partially unfolded antibody gives (@sec-prior). No interaction of hold time and temperature was resolved, and one of the models within 2 AICc units carries one (@sec-near), so the data do not decide whether the two effects add or interact. Within the NOR as characterized the predicted rise across the step is `{python} fx(v_agg["predicted_nor"])` percentage points, with a single-batch bound of `{python} fx(v_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"])` points (@sec-verif). The mechanism also leads one to expect faster aggregation at lower pH, because a more acid pool is further unfolded. No such effect was resolved within the range studied, and the data bound a linear effect within about `{python} fx(max(abs(agg_ph_lo), abs(agg_ph_hi)), 2)` points over that range (@sec-rsm), so within this range the hold time and the temperature determine the aggregate the step adds.

The acidic variants grow with the hold time and with nothing else, by `{python} fx(acid_per60)` percentage points per 60 min. No effect of pH and no effect of temperature was resolved on them in any study of the step. The acid-catalysed hydrolysis of side-chain amides that @sec-prior describes would speed up at a lower pH and at a higher temperature, so it does not explain results that depend on the hold time alone. The rise over the whole hold-time range studied, `{python} fx(acid_rise, 1)` points, is small against the level of about `{python} fx(ACID_T[CENTRE["hold_time"]], 0)` % in the neutralized pool, which is formed upstream, and the attribute stays far inside its criterion at every setting of the step (@sec-criteria).

Fragments grow with the hold time as well. S-VI-OFAT resolved an increase of `{python} fx(OF.loc[FR, "slope_60"], 3)` percentage points per 60 min at the two pH values it compared (@sec-ofat), in the direction cleavage in the hinge region leads one to expect. At that rate a hold at the upper end of the NOR in force adds about `{python} fx(of_frag120, 2)` points. The attribute leaves `{python} fx(fr_margin)` points to its criterion (@sec-criteria). No effect of pH and no effect of temperature on fragments was resolved in any study.

# Design space {#sec-ds}

The design space of the step is the region of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature over which every attribute with a criterion at this step meets it. PCP-006 §7.6 states how it is drawn. It was evaluated on a grid of `{python} grid_n` levels of each factor over the ranges studied, `{python} f"{DSG['n_points']:,}"` points in all, with each output judged on the statistic @sec-stats defines for it. Aggregate is inside when both ends of the `{python} PI` % prediction interval of a single run lie within its criterion at manufacturing scale, and the XMuLV log reduction is inside when its mean prediction reaches the claim.

Of the region studied, `{python} fx(100 * DSG["fraction"], 1)` % meets the criteria of the two outputs that have an adequate model. XMuLV clearance alone rejects `{python} fx(100 * DSG["per_response"][X], 1)` % of the grid, and aggregate rejects none of it. The region is therefore bounded by the clearance claim and not by product quality, and its boundary is the contour drawn in @fig-xmulv. Judging both outputs on their mean predictions gives the same region, because aggregate stays far from its criterion at every point of the grid, so the choice of statistic does not move this boundary. Acidic variants and fragments have no adequate model, so neither draws a boundary. Every measured result of both attributes meets its criterion across the designs, which span the whole region studied, and the region is not constrained by either attribute on that evidence.

The NOR in force lies inside the design space, with the margins @sec-nor gives, and the region studied is the knowledge space of this report. Movement within the design space is not a change from a regulatory filing perspective, as ICH Q8(R2) states, and is assessed under the quality system of ICH Q10 [@ichq10]. A move outside the NOR but inside the design space needs a prospective risk assessment under that system. A move outside the region studied has no evidence in this report and needs new characterization data.

Two limitations apply to the region. The models were fitted in the scale-down model and the spiking model of the step, and the clearance boundary rests on the spiking model, whose representativeness is argued in @sec-sdm rather than measured at scale. The boundary is drawn on the mean predicted log reduction, so at the boundary itself a single batch falls below the claim about half the time, and the step is operated at the set-point with the margin @sec-nor states.

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par-top}

## The acceptance basis {#sec-iac}

A drug substance criterion does not say what the output of an upstream step must meet. Each output of this step is therefore judged against an intermediate acceptance criterion, which PCMP-001 §7.3 derives by carrying the drug substance criterion backward through the train with the worst case that each downstream step showed on the platform, the lowest clearance factor for a step that removes the attribute and the largest increase for a step that adds to it. No margin is applied. An attribute that no downstream step changes keeps its drug substance criterion. @tbl-iac gives the four criteria of this step and their derivation.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation([UO], label="tbl-iac").show()
```

Aggregate in the neutralized pool must not exceed `{python} fx(crit_agg)` % HMW. Cation exchange is the only step after this one that is credited with removing aggregate, so the criterion is the drug substance criterion of `{python} fx(ds_agg)` % multiplied by the clearance factor of cation exchange. Within its NOR, cation exchange cleared less aggregate than its platform worst case, so the one-sided `{python} VB` % prediction bound of a single cation exchange batch, a clearance factor of `{python} fx(cex_fold_agg)`, replaced the platform value, and the a priori criterion of `{python} fx(agg_apriori, 1)` % tightened to the value in @tbl-iac. That analysis is in PCR-007, the characterization report of cation exchange. Fragments must not exceed `{python} fx(crit_frag)` % by nrCE-SDS, which is the drug substance criterion of `{python} fx(ds_frag)` % carried back through the platform worst case of cation exchange, `{python} fx(cex_fold_frag)`-fold. Acidic variants must lie within `{python} fx(acid_lo, 1)` to `{python} fx(acid_hi, 1)` %, the drug substance criterion, because no downstream step is credited with a change in them, and both ends apply. XMuLV clearance must reach the platform claim of the step, `{python} fx(claim)` log~10~.

The criteria were derived after the studies ran, in PCMP-001 Version 2.0. That is acceptable because the derivation uses no result of the studies it judges. The drug substance criteria come from the CQA register, and the downstream worst cases come from the platform history of X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab. A-Mab data enter a criterion only where verification replaced a platform worst case with the prediction bound of a single batch of the same downstream step, which is what happened to the aggregate criterion of this step. @tbl-criteria-change compares them with the limits of Version 1.0.

The cumulative requirement for XMuLV is met by three claims. Low-pH inactivation claims `{python} fx(claim)` log~10~, anion exchange `{python} fx(claim_aex)` log~10~ and virus filtration `{python} fx(claim_vf)` log~10~, which sum to `{python} fx(claims_sum)` log~10~ against a requirement of `{python} fx(xmulv_req, 1)` log~10~. The surplus is `{python} fx(claims_sum - xmulv_req)` log~10~, so a shortfall at this step larger than that cannot be made up by the other two claims. PCMR-001 consolidates the cumulative claim.

Every output meets its criterion. For aggregate those limits are `{python} fx(PI_LO_A)` to `{python} fx(PI_HI_A)` % HMW at manufacturing scale, against a criterion of `{python} fx(crit_agg)` %, which leaves `{python} fx(crit_agg - UPL_A)` percentage points. The upper limit falls at `{python} wu("ph", g(WC_A["settings"]["ph"]))`, `{python} wu("hold_time", g(WC_A["settings"]["hold_time"]))` and `{python} wu("temperature", g(WC_A["settings"]["temperature"]))`, the longest hold and the warmest temperature of the NOR. At the set-point the model predicts `{python} fx(float(D.to_mfg(UO, A, D.predict(UO, A, natural={k: SP[k] for k in FAC}))[0]))` % HMW. The conclusion holds with the offset of the scale-down model at either end of its interval, as @sec-sdm reports.

The XMuLV log reduction is predicted at `{python} fx(X_SP)` log~10~ at the set-point. The lowest mean prediction over the NOR in force is `{python} fx(WC_X["predicted"])` log~10~, at `{python} wu("ph", g(WC_X["settings"]["ph"]))`, `{python} wu("hold_time", g(WC_X["settings"]["hold_time"]))` and `{python} wu("temperature", g(WC_X["settings"]["temperature"]))`, the highest pH, the shortest hold and the coolest temperature of the NOR. The claim of `{python} fx(claim)` log~10~ is met there, with `{python} fx(WC_X["predicted"] - claim)` log~10~ to spare. The prediction interval of a single batch at that combination runs from `{python} fx(WC_X["pi_low"])` to `{python} fx(WC_X["pi_high"])` log~10~, so a single spiked run at the least favourable corner can fall below the claim. That interval is reported for information (@sec-stats). Of the `{python} len(MEAS[X])` individual results of the designs, `{python} x_below` lie below the claim. Every run of both designs was made at a corner, a face centre or the centre of the region studied, so none was made inside the NOR in force, and the lowest of those results was measured at `{python} wu("ph", g(RNG["ph"][1]))`, `{python} wu("hold_time", g(RNG["hold_time"][0]))` and `{python} wu("temperature", g(RNG["temperature"][0]))`, outside the NOR in every factor.

Acidic variants and fragments have no adequate model, so each is judged on its measured results, as PCMP-001 §7.2 requires. The acidic variants of the designs run from `{python} fx(MEAS[AC].min(), 1)` to `{python} fx(MEAS[AC].max(), 1)` % at manufacturing scale, inside the criterion of `{python} fx(acid_lo, 1)` to `{python} fx(acid_hi, 1)` % at both ends and far from either. The conclusion holds with the offset at either end of its interval. The fragments of the response-surface design run from `{python} fx(MEAS[FR].min())` to `{python} fx(MEAS[FR].max())` %, against a criterion of `{python} fx(crit_frag)` %. The designs span the whole region studied, which contains the NOR, so these results cover the NOR as well. They are stated at the scale of the laboratory model for fragments, whose offset was not measured (@sec-sdm).

## Hold of the neutralized pool {#sec-hold}

PCP-006 planned no hold study, and Version 1.0 of this report had no hold result. The neutralized pool was therefore held during the Version 2.0 re-analysis, from `{python} win("S-VI-HLD")`, registered as PD-006-05, the hold study of the neutralized pool. One pool made at the set-points as characterized was held at `{python} join_and(H_TEMPS)` for `{python} H_DAYS` days, and aggregate, acidic variants and fragments were measured at every time point. @tbl-hold-viral-inactivation gives the results.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.hold_stability(UO, label="tbl-hold-viral-inactivation").show()
```

PCP-006 sets no hold criterion. A held pool must meet the criteria of @tbl-iac when it enters cation exchange, as PCMP-001 §7.3 requires, so what has to be judged is what the hold adds to the level the step delivers. The approach is the following. The highest level expected to enter the hold is taken from the step itself, which is the upper single-batch limit over the NOR for aggregate and the highest measured result for the two outputs with no model, and the largest increase measured over the hold is added to it. No plan sets that approach, and it was chosen after the hold results were known, which PD-006-05 records (@sec-record).

Aggregate rose by at most `{python} fx(max(HCH[A]["up"]), 3)` percentage points over `{python} H_DAYS` days, more than the `{python} fx(HCH[A]["d0"], 3)` points between the two aliquots at day 0, so the increase is resolved. Added to the `{python} fx(UPL_A)` % expected to enter the hold it gives `{python} fx(h_agg)` %, against the criterion of `{python} fx(crit_agg)` %. Fragments rose by at most `{python} fx(max(HCH[FR]["up"]), 3)` points, against `{python} fx(HCH[FR]["d0"], 3)` points between the day-0 aliquots, which gives `{python} fx(h_frag)` % against the criterion of `{python} fx(crit_frag)` %. The acidic variants rose by `{python} fx(max(HCH[AC]["up"]), 2)` points at `{python} H_TEMPS[1]`, which gives `{python} fx(h_acid_hi, 1)` % against the upper limit of `{python} fx(acid_hi, 1)` %, and the lowest level expected to enter the hold is `{python} fx(h_acid_lo, 1)` % against the lower limit of `{python} fx(acid_lo, 1)` %. At `{python} H_TEMPS[0]` no change in acidic variants was resolved against the `{python} fx(HCH[AC]["d0"], 2)` points between the day-0 aliquots. The upper limits for aggregate and fragments are met, and so are both ends of the acidic variant criterion.

The pool itself is also to be read as it was measured. @tbl-hold-viral-inactivation gives `{python} fx(float(H[H.day == 0]["hmw_pct"].min()), 2)` to `{python} fx(float(H[H.day == 0]["hmw_pct"].max()), 2)` % HMW and `{python} fx(h_d0_raw[0], 1)` to `{python} fx(h_d0_raw[1], 1)` % acidic variants at day 0, and `{python} fx(h_acid_max, 1)` % acidic variants at day `{python} H_DAYS` at `{python} H_TEMPS[1]`, the highest level of the study. At manufacturing scale those acidic variant values are `{python} fx(h_d0_mfg[0], 1)` to `{python} fx(h_d0_mfg[1], 1)` % at day 0 and `{python} fx(h_acid_max_mfg, 1)` % at the end, inside the criterion at both ends. The day-0 values lie above every acidic variant result of S-VI-OFAT, which ran in the same days and reached `{python} fx(float(of_acid_mfg.max()), 1)` % at most at manufacturing scale (@sec-ofat). The record gives no reason for the difference. The conclusion covers that one pool, at the two temperatures and over the time tested. The study used material made at the set-points as characterized, so it bounds what a hold adds to a pool of that composition and not what it adds to a pool from the edge of the NOR.

## The ranges of the three factors {#sec-par}

@tbl-par gives the PAR of each factor for XMuLV clearance, as PCMP-001 §6.4 defines the two analyses. The first analysis scans the factor across its range studied with the other two at their set-points and compares the mean prediction with the criterion. The second varies the other two within their NORs, as @sec-stats sets out, and compares the central 95 % of the simulated batches with the criterion for a quality attribute and the lowest mean prediction among the NOR combinations with the claim for viral clearance. The second analysis is the one that supports a claim, because the range must hold while the rest of the operating point moves within its NOR.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_pt = PT[PT["CQA"] == LAB[X]].copy()
assert len(_pt) == len(FAC) and (_pt["Basis"] == "selected model").all()
_pt["Parameter"] = [f"{p_} ({u_})" for p_, u_ in zip(_pt["Parameter"], _pt["Unit"])]
_pt["Criterion"] = "≥ " + fx(claim)
T.frame(_pt[["Parameter", "Char. range", "Criterion", "PAR (set-point)", "PAR (NOR)"]],
        "Proven acceptable ranges of the three factors for XMuLV clearance, in natural units, from the "
        "selected response-surface model.", "tbl-par",
        header={"Char. range": "Range\nstudied", "PAR (set-point)": "PAR\n(set-point)",
                "PAR (NOR)": "PAR\n(NOR)"},
        align=["P{4.2cm}", "P{2.4cm}", "P{2.4cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "P{2.6cm}"],
        notes=[("", "Range studied, the characterized range. Criterion, the claim of the step in log10. "
                    "PAR (set-point), the first analysis of PCMP-001 §6.4. PAR (NOR), the NOR-propagated "
                    "analysis, which is the one that supports the claim."),
               ("", "A range that reaches the end of the range studied is reported as reaching it, and no "
                    "claim is made beyond it. Aggregate, acidic variants and fragments are not shown. The "
                    "text gives their ranges.")]).show()
```

One edge of each range comes from XMuLV clearance. Its PAR is `{python} wu("ph", PARX["ph"])`, `{python} wu("hold_time", PARX["hold_time"])` and `{python} wu("temperature", PARX["temperature"])`. The upper pH edge and the lower hold-time and temperature edges are where the mean predicted log reduction falls to the claim. The other three edges are the ends of the ranges studied, so they are where the study stopped and not where the criterion fails. Aggregate meets its criterion across the whole range studied of each factor on the selected model, so its PAR is the range studied in all three. Acidic variants and fragments have no adequate model, so neither sets a PAR. Their measured results meet their criteria throughout the designs, which span the region studied (@sec-criteria). The range carried into the control strategy is therefore the XMuLV range of each factor. Those ranges widen if run `{python} INF5["run"]` is deleted from the design (@sec-influence), and the ranges reported here are the narrower ones.

@fig-par-xmulv and @fig-par-agg show the two analyses for one parameter of each modelled attribute, inactivation pH for the XMuLV log reduction and hold time for aggregate. Each is the parameter with the largest coefficient in its model, although for XMuLV clearance the coefficients of pH and hold time are of the same size (@sec-rsm).

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-xmulv
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range of the inactivation pH for the XMuLV log reduction. Left, the mean prediction with the other two factors fixed. Right, the median and the range of mean predictions over the NOR combinations of hold time and temperature. In both panels the band labelled PAR in the legend is the acceptable range of the pH, the band labelled NOR is the NOR in force, the dotted vertical line is the set-point and the dashed horizontal line is the claim of the step."
D.fig_par(UO, X, gov_x)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-agg
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range of the hold time for aggregate, at manufacturing scale. Left, the mean prediction with the other two factors fixed. Right, the median and the 95 % prediction interval of a single batch with pH and temperature varying within their NORs. The band labelled PAR in the legend is the acceptable range, the band labelled NOR is the NOR in force and the dotted vertical line is the set-point. The dashed horizontal line is the criterion of the attribute, and the axis reaches it, so the predicted rise along the hold time is a shallow slope at the foot of the panel."
D.fig_par(UO, A, gov_a)
plt.show()
```

In the left panel of @fig-par-xmulv the mean predicted log reduction falls through the claim inside the range studied, and in the right panel the band is the range of mean predictions over the NOR combinations of hold time and temperature. In @fig-par-agg the predicted aggregate rises from `{python} fx(AGG_H[RNG["hold_time"][0]])` % at `{python} g(RNG["hold_time"][0])` min to `{python} fx(AGG_H[RNG["hold_time"][1]])` % at `{python} g(RNG["hold_time"][1])` min with the other two factors at their set-points, a rise of `{python} fx(agg_h_rise)` percentage points, against a criterion of `{python} fx(crit_agg)` %. The axis of the panel reaches the criterion, so that rise appears as a shallow slope and the shaded acceptable region covers the whole panel.

The ranges above and the design space of @sec-ds are two views of the same models. A PAR is one factor scanned with the others inside their NORs, and the design space is the region in all three factors at once. The control strategy uses the NOR, which lies inside both.

## The set-points and ranges in force, and the decisions behind them {#sec-nor}

The studies were planned against the set-points and NORs of PCP-006 Version 1.0 and run around them. Against those values the XMuLV claim was not met. The lowest mean predicted log reduction over the NOR as characterized was `{python} fx(WC_Xc["predicted"])` log~10~, at `{python} wu("ph", g(WC_Xc["settings"]["ph"]))`, `{python} wu("hold_time", g(WC_Xc["settings"]["hold_time"]))` and `{python} wu("temperature", g(WC_Xc["settings"]["temperature"]))`, against the claim of `{python} fx(claim)` log~10~. At the former pH set-point of `{python} spc_t["ph"]` the lowest mean prediction over that NOR is already `{python} fx(float(D.predict(UO, X, natural={"ph": SPc["ph"], "hold_time": NORc["hold_time"][0], "temperature": NORc["temperature"][0]})[0]))` log~10~, so no PAR of any factor contained that NOR, and PCP-006 §8 rule 4 requires that to be reported as no PAR. @tbl-nor-change gives the values the studies were run around and the values in force.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_nr = pd.DataFrame([{"Parameter": NAME[k], "Unit": UNIT[k], "Set-point as characterized": g(SPc[k]),
                     "NOR as characterized": rg(*NORc[k]), "Set-point in force": g(SP[k]),
                     "NOR in force": rg(*NOR[k]),
                     "Change": join_and([x for x in [("set-point " + ("moved" if SP[k] != SPc[k] else "unchanged")),
                                                     ("NOR " + (NOR_CHANGE[k] or "unchanged"))]])}
                    for k in FAC])
T.frame(_nr, "Set-points and normal operating ranges as characterized and in force.", "tbl-nor-change",
        header={"Set-point as characterized": "Set-point as\ncharacterized", "NOR as characterized": "NOR as\ncharacterized",
                "Set-point in force": "Set-point\nin force", "NOR in force": "NOR in\nforce"},
        align=["P{2.6cm}", "l", "R{2.4cm}", "P{2.2cm}", "R{1.9cm}", "P{1.7cm}", "P{2.6cm}"],
        notes=[("", "As characterized, the value the studies were planned against and run around. In "
                    "force, the value this revision adopts. The A-Mab concentration is unchanged, and "
                    "its NOR equals the range studied.")]).show()
```

Three decisions produced the values in force, each taken after the results of the designs were known. The pH at which the claim is lost depends on the shortest hold and the coolest temperature of the NOR, because a longer and warmer hold raises the log reduction. The two decisions that narrowed the hold-time NOR therefore moved that pH, and the decision that re-centred the pH left it where the first had put it.

1. The hold-time NOR was narrowed to begin at the former set-point of `{python} spc_t["hold_time"]`, giving `{python} wu("hold_time", rg(ST1_NOR["hold_time"][0], ST1_NOR["hold_time"][1]))`, and the temperature NOR to `{python} nor_t["temperature"]`. With those ranges the model puts the pH at which the claim is lost at `{python} fx(ST_EDGE[1])`. The pH NOR as characterized reached `{python} fx(ST_OVER1)` pH units beyond it, and the former set-point of `{python} spc_t["ph"]` sat `{python} fx(ST_MARG_SP1)` pH units inside it.
2. The pH set-point was moved to `{python} sp_t["ph"]` and the pH NOR to `{python} nor_t["ph"]`, and the hold-time set-point to `{python} wu("hold_time", g(ST2_SP["hold_time"]))`, the middle of the hold-time NOR of the first decision. A NOR of `{python} MINUS + fx(nor_half_ph)` to +`{python} fx(nor_half_ph)` pH units about the set-point is already tight for pH control at manufacturing scale, so the width of the NOR was kept and the range was placed at the acid end of the NOR as characterized, where the log reduction is larger. The upper pH NOR edge of `{python} wu("ph", g(NOR["ph"][1]))` then had a margin of `{python} fx(ST_MARG2)` pH units to the pH at which the claim is lost. Two studies support the new pH set-point, a hold of the pool at it against the former set-point (@sec-ofat) and cation exchange runs on material inactivated at it (@sec-cex).
3. A margin of `{python} fx(ST_MARG2)` pH units is smaller than the `{python} fx(nor_half_ph)` pH units the NOR itself allows on either side of the set-point, which is about what pH control holds at manufacturing scale. No plan sets a minimum margin, so the size that is enough is a judgement of this report. On that judgement `{python} fx(ST_MARG2)` pH units was not accepted, and the hold-time NOR was narrowed again, to `{python} nor_t["hold_time"]`, with its set-point at the middle of it, `{python} sp_t["hold_time"]`. With the ranges in force the model puts the pH at which the claim is lost at `{python} fx(ST_EDGE[3])`, a margin of `{python} fx(ST_MARG3)` pH units from the upper pH NOR edge, which was accepted. A narrower hold-time NOR moves routine operation toward longer holds, which add aggregate, fragments and acidic variants, so confirmation runs were made at the low end of the pH PAR with hold time and temperature at the upper ends of their NORs (@sec-wc).

Each pH is computed from the selected model at the shortest hold and the coolest temperature of the NOR of that stage. @tbl-par-margins gives the margins of the NOR-propagated analysis of @sec-par.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_mg = pd.DataFrame([{"Factor": NAME[k], "Unit": UNIT[k], "NOR in force": rg(*NOR[k]),
                     "PAR": PARX[k], "Edge of the PAR that binds": lbl,
                     "Margin from the NOR edge": fx(MARG[k], {"ph": 2, "hold_time": 0, "temperature": 1}[k]),
                     "Margin from the set-point": fx(MARG_SP[k], {"ph": 2, "hold_time": 0, "temperature": 1}[k])}
                    for k, lbl in (("ph", "upper"), ("hold_time", "lower"), ("temperature", "lower"))])
T.frame(_mg, "Margins from the NOR in force to the proven acceptable range set by XMuLV clearance.",
        "tbl-par-margins", header={"Edge of the PAR that binds": "Edge of the\nPAR that binds",
                                   "Margin from the NOR edge": "Margin to\nNOR edge",
                                   "Margin from the set-point": "Margin to\nset-point"},
        align=["P{2.8cm}", "l", "l", "l", "P{2.2cm}", "R{1.9cm}", "R{1.9cm}"],
        notes=[("", "PAR, the NOR-propagated proven acceptable range of the factor for XMuLV clearance. "
                    "Margins in the unit of the factor, computed from the PAR edges as printed. The other "
                    "edge of each range is the end of the range studied.")]).show()
```

The NOR in force lies inside the PAR of every attribute, so the step meets every criterion across it (@sec-criteria). The edge of the pH NOR that binds carries a margin of `{python} fx(MARG["ph"])` pH units and the set-point `{python} fx(MARG_SP["ph"])` pH units, both above the `{python} fx(nor_half_ph)` pH units of the judgement above.

These changes are changes to the control strategy of the step. They were decided on the data of the studies reported here, which means the ranges in force were chosen after the results were seen, and the confirmation runs of @sec-wc were made for that reason. The comparisons with the platform worst cases (@sec-verif) and with Version 1.0 use the NOR and set-points as characterized, which the studies were planned against, so that no change of a NOR moves a criterion or a Version 1.0 number.

### Quality attributes at the new pH set-point {#sec-ofat}

PCP-006 planned no study at the Version 2.0 set-points. The response-surface design covers pH `{python} g(RNG["ph"][0])` to `{python} g(RNG["ph"][1])`, so it predicts the attributes at the new set-point rather than measuring them there. Study S-VI-OFAT therefore held the pool at `{python} sp_t["ph"]` against `{python} spc_t["ph"]` as a control, at `{python} g(of_temp)` °C, over hold times of `{python} join_and([g(h) for h in of_hold])` min, in duplicate at each pH and hold time, `{python} of_n` runs per pH. It ran from `{python} win("S-VI-OFAT")` and is registered as PD-006-01, the study at the new pH set-point. @tbl-vi-ofat gives every result and @tbl-vi-ofat-effects the analysis.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.vi_ofat(label="tbl-vi-ofat").show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.ofat_effects(label="tbl-vi-ofat-effects").show()
```

Each attribute was analysed on the pH, as a two-level factor, and the hold time, so the difference between the two pH values is estimated at any hold time. The interaction was tested separately, and the three pH p-values were adjusted by Holm's method, because three attributes were tested.

Aggregate and fragments rose with hold time, and for neither was an effect of pH detected. Aggregate rose `{python} fx(OF.loc[A, "slope_60"], 3)` percentage points per 60 min (`{python} pv(OF.loc[A, "p_slope"])`) and fragments `{python} fx(OF.loc[FR, "slope_60"], 3)` points per 60 min (`{python} pv(OF.loc[FR, "p_slope"])`). The difference between the two pH values was `{python} fx(OF.loc[A, "ph_effect"], 3)` points for aggregate, with a 95 % confidence interval from `{python} fx(OF.loc[A, "ph_lo"], 3)` to `{python} fx(OF.loc[A, "ph_hi"], 3)` points, and `{python} fx(OF.loc[FR, "ph_effect"], 3)` points for fragments, from `{python} fx(OF.loc[FR, "ph_lo"], 3)` to `{python} fx(OF.loc[FR, "ph_hi"], 3)` points. Neither reached significance after adjustment, and each interval is narrow against the margin of the attribute to its criterion.

The acidic variants were `{python} fx(abs(OF.loc[AC, "ph_effect"]))` percentage points lower at `{python} sp_t["ph"]` than at `{python} spc_t["ph"]`, with a 95 % confidence interval from `{python} fx(abs(OF.loc[AC, "ph_hi"]))` to `{python} fx(abs(OF.loc[AC, "ph_lo"]))` points, and the difference is significant after adjustment (`{python} pv(OF.loc[AC, "p_ph_holm"])`). Three features place it before the hold rather than in it. The difference was already `{python} fx(abs(OF.loc[AC, "diff_t0"]))` points at time 0, in the pH-adjusted load before any hold, where a hold effect cannot yet have acted. It did not grow with hold time (`{python} pv(OF.loc[AC, "p_interaction"])`), and a reaction driven by the hold pH would. The response-surface model of the attribute carries hold time alone and no pH term (@sec-rsm). The difference is `{python} fx(abs(OF.loc[AC, "ph_effect"]))` percentage points against a criterion `{python} fx(acid_hi - acid_lo, 1)` points wide, and the lowest result at the new set-point, `{python} fx(OF_MFG["all"]["acid"].min(), 1)` % at manufacturing scale, lies `{python} fx(OF_MFG["all"]["acid"].min() - acid_lo, 1)` points above the lower limit of `{python} fx(acid_lo, 1)` %. No plan sets a size at which a significant difference of this attribute would matter, so calling this one small against its criterion is a judgement of this report.

Every result at the new pH set-point meets the criterion of its attribute. Over the hold times of the study up to the upper end of the hold-time NOR in force, which are `{python} join_and([g(h) for h in of_hold if h <= NOR["hold_time"][1]])` min, the results run from `{python} fx(OF_MFG["all"]["agg"].min())` to `{python} fx(OF_MFG["all"]["agg"].max())` % HMW for aggregate at manufacturing scale, against `{python} fx(crit_agg)` %, from `{python} fx(OF_MFG["all"]["frag"].min())` to `{python} fx(OF_MFG["all"]["frag"].max())` % for fragments, against `{python} fx(crit_frag)` %, and from `{python} fx(OF_MFG["all"]["acid"].min(), 1)` to `{python} fx(OF_MFG["all"]["acid"].max(), 1)` % for acidic variants at manufacturing scale, against `{python} fx(acid_lo, 1)` to `{python} fx(acid_hi, 1)` %. At the two hold times inside the NOR in force, `{python} join_and([g(h) for h in oft_hold_nor])` min, aggregate runs from `{python} fx(OF_MFG["nor"]["agg"].min())` to `{python} fx(OF_MFG["nor"]["agg"].max())` %, fragments from `{python} fx(OF_MFG["nor"]["frag"].min())` to `{python} fx(OF_MFG["nor"]["frag"].max())` % and acidic variants from `{python} fx(OF_MFG["nor"]["acid"].min(), 1)` to `{python} fx(OF_MFG["nor"]["acid"].max(), 1)` %. Each conclusion for aggregate and acidic variants holds with the offset at either end of its interval. The study measured no viral clearance, so it supports the new set-point for product quality only, and the clearance there comes from the model (@sec-criteria). Fragments were measured by nrCE-SDS in this study, as @tbl-methods-by-study shows.

### Cation exchange on material from the step at the new pH set-point {#sec-cex}

The criteria of this step assume that cation exchange clears aggregate and fragments from its load by at least a fixed factor (@sec-iac). PCP-006 planned no downstream verification. Study S-CEX-VER therefore ran cation exchange at set-point on material from the step at its new pH set-point, inactivated at `{python} wu("ph", g(CVC["load_from"]["ph"]))` for `{python} wu("hold_time", g(CVC["load_from"]["hold_time"]))` at `{python} wu("temperature", g(CVC["load_from"]["temperature"]))`, the longest hold and the warmest temperature of the NOR in force. It ran from `{python} win("S-CEX-VER")` and is registered as PD-006-02, the cation exchange verification runs.

The number of runs was fixed before the runs were made, by the simulation in @tbl-cex-verification-n. The clearance factor of a run is the load level divided by the pool level, and its logarithm is the log reduction value of that run. A verification passes when the one-sided `{python} VB` % lower confidence bound of the mean log reduction value of the runs reaches the clearance factor the criteria rely on. The simulation gives the smallest number of runs, at most `{python} int(CVC["n_max"])`, with a probability of at least `{python} fx(CVC["power"])` of passing when cation exchange clears as its own data show.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.cex_verification_n(label="tbl-cex-verification-n").show()
```

The two probability columns give the chance of passing when cation exchange clears as its own data show and when it clears exactly the factor the criteria rely on. Aggregate needs `{python} int(CV.loc["aggregates_hmw", "n_required"])` run and fragments `{python} int(CV.loc["fragments_lmw", "n_required"])`, because the clearance factor in the cation exchange data exceeds the required factor by much more for aggregate than for fragments, `{python} fx(CV.loc["aggregates_hmw", "f_data"])` against `{python} fx(CV.loc["aggregates_hmw", "f_required"])` and `{python} fx(CV.loc["fragments_lmw", "f_data"])` against `{python} fx(CV.loc["fragments_lmw", "f_required"])`. The larger of the two needs decided the study, so `{python} cv_n` runs were made. @tbl-cex-verification gives them.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.cex_verification_runs(label="tbl-cex-verification").show()
```

Both attributes passed. Cation exchange cleared aggregate by a clearance factor of `{python} fx(CV.loc["aggregates_hmw", "fold_gmean"])` at the geometric mean of the three runs, with a lower bound of `{python} fx(CV.loc["aggregates_hmw", "fold_bound"])` against the `{python} fx(CV.loc["aggregates_hmw", "f_required"])` the criteria rely on, and fragments by a factor of `{python} fx(CV.loc["fragments_lmw", "fold_gmean"])` with a lower bound of `{python} fx(CV.loc["fragments_lmw", "fold_bound"])` against `{python} fx(CV.loc["fragments_lmw", "f_required"])`. Every run cleared more than the required factor for both attributes. The cation exchange pool also met the criteria of that step, at most `{python} fx(CV.loc["aggregates_hmw", "pool_max"])` % HMW against `{python} fx(cex_crit_agg)` % and `{python} fx(CV.loc["fragments_lmw", "pool_max"])` % fragments against `{python} fx(cex_crit_frag)` %. The material from the step at its new pH set-point therefore behaves at cation exchange as the criteria of this step assume.

### Confirmation runs at the low end of the pH PAR {#sec-wc}

The revision of the hold-time NOR moves routine operation toward longer holds, which is the direction that adds aggregate and fragments. PCP-006 planned no study at the Version 2.0 NOR. Study S-VI-WC therefore held the pool at `{python} wu("ph", g(wc_set["ph"]))`, the lower end of the range studied and of the pH PAR, for `{python} wu("hold_time", g(wc_set["hold_time"]))` at `{python} wu("temperature", g(wc_set["temperature"]))`, the upper ends of the hold-time and temperature NORs in force. The hold-time and temperature PARs reach further than those two settings, to `{python} wu("hold_time", g(PE["hold_time"][1]))` and `{python} wu("temperature", g(PE["temperature"][1]))`, so the runs bound what routine operation can deliver and not what the PAR allows. Each hold was followed by a cation exchange run at set-point. The study ran from `{python} win("S-VI-WC")`, with `{python} int(WS["n_runs"].iloc[0])` runs, as many as the cation exchange verification, and is registered as PD-006-03, the confirmation runs at the low end of the pH PAR.

Product quality met every criterion of the step. At manufacturing scale aggregate ran from `{python} fx(WC_MFG["agg"].min())` to `{python} fx(WC_MFG["agg"].max())` % HMW against `{python} fx(crit_agg)` %, and acidic variants from `{python} fx(WC_MFG["acid"].min(), 1)` to `{python} fx(WC_MFG["acid"].max(), 1)` % against `{python} fx(acid_lo, 1)` to `{python} fx(acid_hi, 1)` %. Each of those verdicts holds with the offset at either end of its interval. Fragments, which have no measured offset, ran from `{python} fx(WC_MFG["frag"].min())` to `{python} fx(WC_MFG["frag"].max())` % at the scale of the laboratory model, against `{python} fx(crit_frag)` %. @tbl-vi-worst-case gives the cation exchange runs on that material and the decision on each clearance factor, by the rule of @sec-cex.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.vi_worst_case_runs(label="tbl-vi-worst-case").show()
```

For aggregate the rule is met. Cation exchange cleared aggregate by a clearance factor of `{python} fx(WS.loc["aggregates_hmw", "fold_gmean"])` at the geometric mean, with a lower bound of `{python} fx(WS.loc["aggregates_hmw", "fold_bound"])` against the `{python} fx(WS.loc["aggregates_hmw", "f_required"])` the criteria rely on.

For fragments the rule is not met. Each of the three runs cleared more than the required factor, from `{python} fx(min(WS.loc["fragments_lmw", "folds"]))` to `{python} fx(max(WS.loc["fragments_lmw", "folds"]))` against `{python} fx(WS.loc["fragments_lmw", "f_required"])`, and the geometric mean was `{python} fx(WS.loc["fragments_lmw", "fold_gmean"])`. The one-sided `{python} VB` % lower confidence bound of the mean log reduction value was `{python} fx(WS.loc["fragments_lmw", "fold_bound"])`, below the required factor, so the rule the simulation of @sec-cex fixed before the runs is not met. The three runs are not pooled with the `{python} cv_n` runs of S-CEX-VER, which were made on different material, and no rule of the analysis was changed once the result was known.

The failure was accepted on its risk, and PD-006-03 records the grounds. Fragments in the pool leaving the hold reached `{python} fx(WC_MFG["frag"].max())` % at most, which already meets the drug substance criterion of `{python} fx(ds_frag)` %, so the drug substance would meet that criterion even if cation exchange cleared no fragments at all. The risk of a lower fragment clearance at cation exchange therefore falls on the producer and not on the patient. Fragments are tested by nrCE-SDS at release, so an excursion would be detected on the drug substance itself. The cation exchange pool of these runs also met the fragment criterion of that step, at most `{python} fx(WS.loc["fragments_lmw", "pool_max"])` % against `{python} fx(cex_crit_frag)` %. None of the `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` simulated batches of the integrated model falls outside the drug substance criterion for fragments, so that probability is below `{python} fx(100 * poos_bound, 2)` % at one-sided 95 % confidence (@sec-capability). No criterion of this report rests on the failed bound. The fragment criterion of this step uses the platform worst case of cation exchange, not these runs (@sec-iac), and fragments at this step are judged on their measured results. The acceptance was decided after the result was known.

## A-Mab concentration {#sec-uni}

A-Mab concentration was assessed one factor at a time, for the reasons @sec-prior gives. Study S-VI-UNI ran the hold at `{python} g(conc_lo)` and `{python} g(conc_hi)` g/L in duplicate, with the other three parameters at their set-points as characterized. PCP-006 §6.4 required aggregate, acidic variants and the XMuLV log reduction on every run. The study measured aggregate and acidic variants only (PD-006-07), and the clearance was measured later in the confirmation study S-VI-UNI2 (PD-006-06). @tbl-uni gives both studies.

```{python}

for _, r_ in _u.iterrows():

                  "Acidic variants, %": fx(float(D.to_mfg(UO, AC, r_["acidic_variants"])), 1),
                  "XMuLV LRF, log10": "n.t." if pd.isna(r_["xmulv_lrf"]) else fx(r_["xmulv_lrf"])})
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_rows), "A-Mab concentration at both ends of its range, in the study of the "

        merge=["Study", "A-Mab concentration (g/L)"],

                "Acidic variants, %": "Acidic\nvariants, %", "XMuLV LRF, log10": "XMuLV LRF,\nlog10"},
        align=["l", "R{2.2cm}", "c", "R{2.2cm}", "R{2.2cm}", "R{2.2cm}"],
```
