For aggregate and acidic variants no effect of the concentration was detected within the range studied. In S-VI-UNI aggregate was `{python} fx(u1_agg["high"] - u1_agg["low"], 3)` percentage points higher at `{python} g(conc_hi)` g/L than at `{python} g(conc_lo)` g/L, with a 95 % confidence interval from `{python} fx(u1_d_lo, 3)` to `{python} fx(u1_d_hi, 3)` points, and in S-VI-UNI2 `{python} fx(u2_agg_d, 3)` points, with an interval from `{python} fx(u2_agg_lo, 3)` to `{python} fx(u2_agg_hi, 3)` points. Both intervals contain zero, and both are narrow against the margin of `{python} fx(crit_agg - UPL_A)` points between the highest single-batch prediction over the NOR and the criterion. At the scale of the laboratory model the two levels of S-VI-UNI differ by `{python} fx(min(u1_agg_dev.values()), 3)` and `{python} fx(max(u1_agg_dev.values()), 3)` points from the mean of the set-point runs of the qualification study, `{python} fx(sdm_agg_mean)` %, whose own standard deviation is `{python} fx(sdm_agg_sd, 3)` points. The acidic variants gave the same result at every run of S-VI-UNI, `{python} fx(u1_acid, 1)` %, which differs from the mean of the set-point runs of the qualification study by `{python} fx(abs(u1_acid_d))` points, inside the standard deviation of those runs, `{python} fx(sdm_acid_sd)` points. Every result of both studies meets its criterion at manufacturing scale, aggregate at most `{python} fx(max(U1_AGG_MFG.max(), U2_AGG_MFG.max()))` % against `{python} fx(crit_agg)` % and acidic variants from `{python} fx(min(U1_ACID_MFG.min(), U2_ACID_MFG.min()), 1)` to `{python} fx(max(U1_ACID_MFG.max(), U2_ACID_MFG.max()), 1)` % against `{python} fx(acid_lo, 1)` to `{python} fx(acid_hi, 1)` %. The range `{python} wu("protein_conc", rg(conc_lo, conc_hi))` is therefore supported for these two attributes.

The range is not supported for fragments, which neither study measured. PCP-006 §6.4 did not require fragments in the concentration study, the samples of S-VI-UNI were not retained, so no nrCE-SDS result can be obtained for them, and SEC is biased in this matrix (@sec-methods). For that attribute the class of the parameter rests on the cleavage reaction itself. Cleavage in the hinge region is a reaction of each molecule with the solvent, so the fraction of molecules cleaved does not depend on how many of them are present.

Study S-VI-UNI2 measured the XMuLV log reduction at both ends of the range, in duplicate, with the other parameters at their set-points as characterized. It ran from `{python} win("S-VI-UNI2")` and measured no fragments (@sec-methods). The log reduction was `{python} fx(u2_lo)` log~10~ at `{python} g(conc_lo)` g/L and `{python} fx(u2_hi)` log~10~ at `{python} g(conc_hi)` g/L, a difference of `{python} fx(-u2_d)` log~10~ at the high end, with a 95 % confidence interval from `{python} fx(u2_x_lo)` to `{python} fx(u2_x_hi)` log~10~ against a run-to-run standard deviation of `{python} fx(FIT[X]["rmse"])` log~10~ from the response-surface design (`{python} pv(u2_p)`). No effect of the concentration on the inactivation was detected, which is what the hold acting on the envelope of the virus leads one to expect (@sec-prior). Four runs bound that effect loosely. The interval reaches `{python} fx(abs(u2_x_lo))` log~10~ on the side of a loss, which is more than the margin of `{python} fx(WC_X["predicted"] - claim)` log~10~ that the claim has over the NOR, so these data alone cannot exclude a loss of clearance at the high end of the range that would matter. For XMuLV clearance the class of the parameter therefore rests on how the hold acts (@sec-class). All four results lie inside the `{python} PI` % prediction interval of a single run at the set-points as characterized, which runs from `{python} fx(X_SPC[1][0])` to `{python} fx(X_SPC[2][0])` log~10~. Of the four, `{python} u2_n_below` lie below the claim of `{python} fx(claim)` log~10~. The claim is judged on the mean prediction of the model (@sec-stats), and a single spiked run carries the scatter of the infectivity assay.

## Verification of the platform worst cases {#sec-verif}

The criteria of the steps upstream of this one assume that the low-pH hold adds no more aggregate, fragments and acidic variants than it added on the platform. Each assumption was checked on the response-surface models of this step, as PCMP-001 §7.5 requires. The check evaluates the model at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high as characterized, which are the values the studies were planned against, so a later change of a NOR cannot move a criterion. It takes the largest increase the model predicts over those combinations and the one-sided `{python} VB` % prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable of them. Every increase is taken against the aggregate level of the load in the process model at set-point, `{python} fx(FEED_AGG)` % HMW, because the input pool of the designs was not tested (PD-006-08). @tbl-iac-verification gives the three assumptions and the results.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.worst_case_verification([UO], label="tbl-iac-verification").show()
```

The column headed at the edges holds the largest increase measured at the edges of the range studied, against the same reference load. The outcome column applies the definition of PCMP-001 §7.5, under which an assumption is confirmed when the largest increase predicted within the NOR is no larger than the platform value. That definition rests on the model of the attribute, and only the aggregate model is adequate, so the confirmations for fragments and acidic variants carry the limitation @sec-discussion states. Only aggregate moved a criterion.

For aggregate the platform value is an increase of `{python} fx(v_agg["assumed"])` percentage points, the largest increase predicted within the NOR as characterized is `{python} fx(v_agg["predicted_nor"])` points and the bound of a single batch is `{python} fx(v_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"])` points. The bound is better than the platform value, and the selected model of aggregate meets every adequacy criterion of PCMP-001 §7.2. PCMP-001 §7.5 and PCP-006 §7.4 both require that of a model before its bound may replace a platform value. PCP-006 §7.4 also asks whether the bound depends on a single run. It does not. With each run that PCP-006 §7.1 flags for examination deleted in turn, the bound is at most `{python} fx(max(i_["bound"] for i_ in INF[A]))` points, still below the platform value (@sec-influence). The bound therefore replaced the platform value, and the aggregate criteria of the steps upstream of this one were recalculated with it.

The criterion affected is the aggregate criterion of the production bioreactor output. Its a priori value is `{python} fx(brx_apriori, 1)` % HMW. The cation exchange verification tightened it to `{python} fx(brx_tight)` %, and the bound of this step then widened it to `{python} fx(brx_final)` %, which is stricter than the a priori value and wider than the value the cation exchange verification alone would give.

The platform values are increases over a hold of `{python} g(RNG["hold_time"][1])` min, and the bound of this step is the increase within a NOR whose longest hold is `{python} g(NORc["hold_time"][1])` min, so the replacement reflects the shorter hold of the A-Mab NOR and not a more stable product. At a hold of `{python} g(RNG["hold_time"][1])` min, the platform hold, A-Mab added up to `{python} fx(v_agg["observed_edge"])` points, more than the platform value of `{python} fx(v_agg["assumed"])` points. The aggregate model carries no pH term, and the NOR in force ends at the same longest hold and warmest temperature as the NOR as characterized, so the same bound covers the NOR in force. A hold longer than the upper end of the NOR is a departure from the control strategy of the step, handled under the quality system of ICH Q10, and the criterion carries no allowance for one.

The widened criterion is an intermediate criterion at the production bioreactor, and the drug substance criterion for aggregate is unchanged, so the risk of the change falls on the producer and not on the patient. What the downstream steps must clear is the factor the criteria already credit, the aggregate clearance of cation exchange, which @sec-cex verified on material from this step. Aggregate is tested against its drug substance criterion by SEC at release. No simulated batch of the integrated model falls outside that criterion, so the probability is below `{python} fx(100 * poos_bound, 2)` % at one-sided 95 % confidence, and the capability index of the attribute is `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["aggregates_hmw", "Cpk"], 1)` (@sec-capability). PCR-003 argues the widened criterion and its risk for the bioreactor.

For fragments and acidic variants the platform values stand. For fragments the largest increase predicted within the NOR as characterized is `{python} fx(v_frag["predicted_nor"])` points against a platform value of `{python} fx(v_frag["assumed"])` points, and at the edges of the range studied the step added up to `{python} fx(v_frag["observed_edge"])` points, more than the platform value. The bound of a single batch is `{python} fx(v_frag["predicted_nor_bound95"])` points, which is not better than the platform value, so no replacement follows and the platform value stands in the fragment criterion of the Protein A output. At the rate of @sec-ofat, a hold at the upper end of the NOR in force adds about `{python} fx(of_frag120, 2)` points. For acidic variants the largest increase predicted within the NOR is `{python} fx(v_acid["predicted_nor"], 2)` points and the bound is the same value, both better than the platform value of `{python} fx(v_acid["assumed"])` points, and every run at a hold of `{python} g(RNG["hold_time"][1])` min added less than the platform value. The bound still does not replace it, because the model of the attribute fits the results exactly and the adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 cannot be applied to it (@sec-rsm). The acidic variant criteria upstream of this step therefore stay at their a priori values.

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-capability}

Capability at commercial scale comes from the integrated model of the train, which runs `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` simulated batches through every step with each parameter drawn within its NOR in force (PCMP-001 §6.5). @tbl-cap gives the four attributes this step sets or changes.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_cp = []
for k in CK:
    r_ = CAPD.loc[k]
    _cp.append({"Attribute": r_["cqa"], "Criticality": r_["criticality"],
                "Drug substance criterion": (f"≥ {g(r_['acc_low'])}" if r_["spec_type"] == "lower" else
                                             f"≤ {g(r_['acc_high'])}" if r_["spec_type"] == "upper" else
                                             f"{g(r_['acc_low'])}–{g(r_['acc_high'])}") + f" {r_['unit']}",
                "Mean": s3(r_["mean"]), "SD": s3(r_["sd"]), "Cpk": fx(r_["Cpk"]),
                "Against PCMP-001": ("Above target" if r_["Cpk"] >= CPK_TARGET else
                                     "Between minimum and target" if r_["Cpk"] >= CPK_MIN else "Below minimum")})
T.frame(pd.DataFrame(_cp), "Commercial-scale capability of the attributes this step sets or changes, from the "
        "integrated model.", "tbl-cap", align=["P{3.4cm}", "c", "P{3.0cm}", "r", "r", "r", "P{2.6cm}"],
        size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Mean and SD (standard deviation) of the simulated batches in the unit of the criterion. "
                    "Cpk against the nearer limit, the lower of the two one-sided indices for a two-sided "
                    "criterion. Target and minimum from PCMP-001 §7.9.")]).show()
```

Cumulative XMuLV clearance has a capability index of `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["lrv_xmulv", "Cpk"])` against its floor of `{python} fx(xmulv_req, 1)` log~10~, which `{python} cpk_verdict(CAPD.loc["lrv_xmulv", "Cpk"])` (PCMP-001 §7.9). The simulated mean is `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["lrv_xmulv", "mean"], 1)` log~10~ with a standard deviation of `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["lrv_xmulv", "sd"])` log~10~, and the three claimed steps together put the distribution far above the requirement. This step contributes the largest of the three claims (@sec-iac).

Of the attributes the hold can add to, acidic variants have the lowest capability index, `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpk"])`, which `{python} cpk_verdict(CAPD.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpk"])`. PCMP-001 §7.9 calls a value between the two acceptable and asks for the side of the criterion that limits it and the parameters that drive it, which PCMR-001 consolidates. The criterion is two-sided and the index is limited by its lower end, `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpl"])` against `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpu"])` at the upper end. The low-pH hold only raises acidic variants, by `{python} fx(acid_per60)` percentage points per 60 min (@sec-mech), so the step moves the attribute away from the limit that binds. A longer hold would raise the index, and no change of this step is proposed on that ground, because the index is set by the level the production bioreactor forms and by its batch spread. PCR-003 gives that analysis and the mitigation. Aggregate and fragments have indices of `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["aggregates_hmw", "Cpk"], 1)` and `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["fragments_lmw", "Cpk"], 1)`, far above the target. The drug substance mean of aggregate is `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["aggregates_hmw", "mean"])` % against a limit of `{python} fx(ds_agg)` %, and of fragments `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["fragments_lmw", "mean"])` % against `{python} fx(ds_frag)` %, because cation exchange and the steps after it remove both.

The same simulation gives the probability that the drug substance is out of specification. No simulated batch falls outside the drug substance criterion for aggregate or for fragments, so each of those probabilities is below `{python} fx(100 * poos_bound, 2)` % at one-sided 95 % confidence, a bound that covers the sampling of the simulation and not the uncertainty of the integrated model itself. For acidic variants `{python} int(POOS.loc["acidic_variants", "n_oos"])` of `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` batches falls below the lower limit, and the tail probability of a normal distribution with the simulated mean and standard deviation is `{python} fx(100 * float(POOS.loc["acidic_variants", "p_oos_normal"]), 2)` %. For XMuLV clearance no batch falls below the requirement and the normal tail probability is `{python} f"{float(POOS.loc['lrv_xmulv', 'p_oos_normal']) * 1e6:.2f}"` per million.

Three results bound the robustness of the step. The claim holds across the NOR on the selected model, with the margins of @tbl-par-margins. The quality attributes met their criteria in every run of the designs, which span the region studied, and in the confirmation runs at the low end of the pH PAR with hold time and temperature at the upper ends of their NORs (@sec-wc). The one pool that was held met its criteria after `{python} H_DAYS` days at `{python} join_and(H_TEMPS)` (@sec-hold), so a hold of a pool of that composition before cation exchange within that window does not threaten the criteria of the next step.

# Parameter classification {#sec-class}

Each parameter was classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7. A critical process parameter (CPP) has an effect on a CQA that is significant and practically relevant within the characterized range, and a high risk of falling outside its acceptable range in operation. A well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP) has the same kind of effect but a low risk of falling outside that range, because it is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR. A key process parameter (KPP) affects process performance and no CQA, and a general process parameter (GPP) affects neither. Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a numerical threshold for an effect that is practically relevant or for a PAR that is wide against its NOR. Where a class turns on such a size, this report names the judgement and the basis it was taken on. The size of each effect across the PAR and the margin from the PAR to the NOR are given with each class. The classes are in @tbl-params.

- *Inactivation pH (CPP).* A rise in pH across the range studied lowers the XMuLV log reduction by `{python} fx(abs(EFX["ph"]))` log~10~ (`{python} pv(PX["ph"])`), which is `{python} fx(abs(EFX["ph"]) / claim * 100, 0)` % of the claim. Across the PAR of `{python} wu("ph", PARX["ph"])` the same model gives a change of `{python} fx(abs(float(np.diff(D.predict(UO, X, natural={"ph": list(PE["ph"]), "hold_time": [SP["hold_time"]] * 2, "temperature": [SP["temperature"]] * 2}))[0])))` log~10~, so the claim is lost at the upper edge of that range. The pH of a large acidified pool is set by acid addition and mixing, which is the least directly controlled of the three settings, and pH control at manufacturing scale holds about `{python} fx(nor_half_ph)` pH units, the half-width of the NOR itself. The margin from the upper NOR edge to the PAR edge is `{python} fx(MARG["ph"])` pH units, so a drift of the size the NOR allows about the set-point would reach the edge of the PAR. No plan sets the margin at which that risk becomes high, so the class rests on that comparison as a judgement, the same comparison the decisions of @sec-nor were taken on. On it the risk is high and the parameter is a CPP.
- *Hold time (WC-CPP).* A longer hold raises the XMuLV log reduction by `{python} fx(EFX["hold_time"])` log~10~ over the range studied (`{python} pv(PX["hold_time"])`) and aggregate by `{python} fx(EFA["hold_time"], 3)` percentage points over the same range (`{python} pv(PA["hold_time"])`). It also raises the acidic variants by `{python} fx(acid_rise, 1)` points over that range and the fragments by `{python} fx(fr_rise_range, 2)` points at the rate S-VI-OFAT measured (@sec-ofat). Across its PAR of `{python} wu("hold_time", PARX["hold_time"])` the clearance effect is `{python} fx(abs(float(np.diff(D.predict(UO, X, natural={"hold_time": list(PE["hold_time"]), "ph": [SP["ph"]] * 2, "temperature": [SP["temperature"]] * 2}))[0])))` log~10~, and the quality attributes stay inside their criteria across the whole range studied. The effect on a CQA makes the parameter critical. The lower PAR edge lies `{python} g(MARG["hold_time"])` min below the NOR, a margin of `{python} fx(100 * MARG["hold_time"] / (NOR["hold_time"][1] - NOR["hold_time"][0]), 0)` % of the width of the NOR. A hold time is counted by the control system from a defined start, and the largest error of a hold-time record in these studies was the `{python} g(dev_006_01_time_discrepancy_min)` min between the two records of DEV-006-01, which is `{python} fx(MARG["hold_time"] / dev_006_01_time_discrepancy_min, 0)` times smaller than the margin. No plan sets the margin at which the risk becomes low, so the class rests on that comparison as a judgement. On it the risk is low and the parameter is a WC-CPP.
- *Temperature (WC-CPP).* A warmer hold raises the XMuLV log reduction by `{python} fx(EFX["temperature"])` log~10~ over the range studied (`{python} pv(PX["temperature"])`) and aggregate by `{python} fx(EFA["temperature"], 3)` percentage points (`{python} pv(PA["temperature"])`). Across its PAR of `{python} wu("temperature", PARX["temperature"])` the clearance effect is `{python} fx(abs(float(np.diff(D.predict(UO, X, natural={"temperature": list(PE["temperature"]), "ph": [SP["ph"]] * 2, "hold_time": [SP["hold_time"]] * 2}))[0])))` log~10~. The effect on a CQA makes it critical. The lower PAR edge lies `{python} fx(MARG["temperature"], 1)` °C below the NOR, a margin of `{python} fx(100 * MARG["temperature"] / (NOR["temperature"][1] - NOR["temperature"][0]), 0)` % of the width of the NOR, and the hold is held near ambient in a jacketed vessel, so the risk of falling outside the acceptable range is low on the same judgement as the hold time. The temperature term of the XMuLV model depends on run `{python} INF5["run"]`, and without that run the XMuLV model carries no temperature term (@sec-influence). The effect on aggregate does not depend on it. Temperature raises aggregate by `{python} fx(agg_temp_lo, 3)` to `{python} fx(agg_temp_hi, 3)` percentage points over the range studied in every model selected after a deletion, and significantly in each (`{python} pv(agg_temp_p_max)` at its weakest), so the parameter affects a CQA whichever flagged run is left out.
- *A-Mab concentration (GPP).* No effect of the concentration was detected on aggregate, on acidic variants or on the XMuLV log reduction across the whole range studied, which is the whole NOR of the parameter (@sec-uni). For aggregate and acidic variants the concentration studies bound the effect well against the margins to the criteria. For XMuLV clearance they do not. Four runs put the difference at the high end of the range at `{python} fx(-u2_d)` log~10~, with a 95 % confidence interval from `{python} fx(u2_x_lo)` to `{python} fx(u2_x_hi)` log~10~, which reaches further on the side of a loss than the margin of `{python} fx(WC_X["predicted"] - claim)` log~10~ that the claim has over the NOR. Four runs cannot establish the absence of an effect of that size, so for that attribute the class rests not on the absence of a detected effect but on how the hold acts. The acid denatures the envelope of the virus, and the antibody around it neither shields the envelope nor takes part in that reaction (@sec-prior). Neither concentration study measured fragments, so for that attribute the class rests on the cleavage reaction (@sec-uni). On the evidence available the parameter affects no CQA and no performance attribute of the step, so it is a GPP.

The step therefore carries one CPP and two WC-CPPs. A WC-CPP is a critical process parameter with good control capability, so all three are critical and all three are controlled within the limits of the design space.

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-cs}

The step contributes four things to the control strategy of the drug substance process, and PCMR-001 consolidates them with the other steps.

1. *The claim and the ranges that assure it.* The step claims `{python} fx(claim)` log~10~ of XMuLV clearance, which it meets across the NOR in force at the least favourable combination (@sec-criteria). The ranges in force are `{python} nor_t["ph"]`, `{python} nor_t["hold_time"]` and `{python} nor_t["temperature"]`, each inside the PAR by the margin @tbl-par-margins gives. The set-points are `{python} sp_t["ph"]`, `{python} sp_t["hold_time"]` and `{python} sp_t["temperature"]`. Inactivation pH is controlled as a CPP and the other two as WC-CPPs (@sec-class).
2. *Monitoring and testing.* XMuLV clearance cannot be measured in manufacture, so the claim rests on keeping inactivation pH, hold time and temperature within their NORs on every batch. A-Mab concentration is a general process parameter within `{python} wu("protein_conc", rg(conc_lo, conc_hi))` (@sec-uni). Aggregate, fragments and acidic variants have drug substance criteria whose methods the CQA register names (@tbl-cqa), so an excursion that reached the drug substance would be found by the release tests of those attributes.
3. *What this step hands to the next.* The neutralized pool is the load of cation exchange, which removes the aggregate the hold forms. The criteria of this step credit cation exchange with a clearance factor of `{python} fx(cex_fold_agg)` for aggregate and `{python} fx(cex_fold_frag)` for fragments, and @sec-cex verified both on material from the step at its new pH set-point. On the material of the confirmation runs the aggregate factor was verified again, and the rule set for the fragment factor was not met and was accepted on its risk (@sec-wc). One pool of the step, made at the set-points as characterized, was held for up to `{python} H_DAYS` days at `{python} join_and(H_TEMPS)` and stayed inside the criteria (@sec-hold). Cation exchange is characterized under PCR-007.
4. *The attributes other steps control.* The cumulative XMuLV requirement is met by this step together with anion exchange (PCR-008) and virus filtration (PCR-009). MVM clearance is claimed by anion exchange and virus filtration, and this step claims none, because a parvovirus has no lipid envelope for low pH to disrupt. Aggregate and acidic variants are formed in the production bioreactor (PCR-003) and fragments during harvest and clarification (PCR-004), and this step adds a bounded amount to each (@sec-verif). The criteria assume no change in host cell protein across this step, and no clearance of it is claimed here (PCR-005).

One lifecycle control follows from the verification. The bound that widened the aggregate criterion of the production bioreactor output covers holds up to `{python} wu("hold_time", g(NORc["hold_time"][1]))` at up to `{python} wu("temperature", g(NORc["temperature"][1]))` (@sec-verif). A change that extended the hold-time or temperature NOR of this step beyond those ends would take routine manufacture outside the basis of that criterion, and is assessed under the change management system of ICH Q10 [@ichq10].

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The step is understood well enough to be operated and transferred. The three parameters trade against each other along the contour of @fig-xmulv, and no interaction among them was resolved by `{python} n_rsm` runs. Aggregate grows with the hold time and with the temperature, the acidic variants and the fragments with the hold time, and all three stay far inside their criteria across the region studied. What limits the step is not product quality but the clearance claim, which is why the design space of @sec-ds is bounded by the clearance contour and why the ranges in force were set from it.

The ranges in force were decided on these data, after the results were seen (@sec-nor). The evidence that they are safe to operate in is of three kinds. The model predicts the claim at the least favourable combination of the NOR with a margin of `{python} fx(WC_X["predicted"] - claim)` log~10~. The quality attributes were measured at the new pH set-point over hold times from `{python} g(of_hold[0])` to `{python} g(of_hold[-1])` min (@sec-ofat) and at the low end of the pH PAR with hold time and temperature at the upper ends of their NORs (@sec-wc), and every result met its criterion. Cation exchange was run on material from both of those conditions and cleared aggregate as the criteria assume.

Confidence in the scale-down model is highest for the two outputs the qualification compared at both scales. The offsets of aggregate and acidic variants are small, their intervals contain zero, and the conclusion over the NOR is the same at either end of both intervals, so the model is qualified for both (@sec-sdm). Six limitations bound what this report claims.

1. *Fragments and viral clearance were not compared at both scales.* Their offsets are unknown rather than zero. For fragments the conclusion rests on the assumption that cleavage in the hinge region depends on pH, time and temperature and not on the size of the vessel, and the margin of `{python} fx(fr_margin)` percentage points to the criterion bounds what the assumption can cost. For viral clearance it rests on the spiking model, in which the matrix, the pH and the temperature are those of manufacture and only the volume differs.
2. *The log reduction carries the variability of a cell-based assay.* Its coefficient of variation at the centre points is `{python} fx(CVR.loc[LAB[X], "%CV"], 1)` %, the largest of any response. The claim is judged on the mean prediction (@sec-stats), and a single spiked run at the least favourable corner of the NOR can fall below it (@sec-criteria). The screening and the response-surface design also gave different pH effects on the same corner settings (@sec-screening), which bounds how precisely one campaign of spiked runs fixes that effect.
3. *Two results depend on one run.* Both selected models meet every adequacy criterion, and no conclusion over the NOR changed when a flagged run was deleted (@sec-influence). The temperature term of the XMuLV model and the width of the XMuLV PARs both depend on run `{python} INF5["run"]`, so the margins of @tbl-par-margins are the conservative reading of `{python} n_rsm` runs rather than a result a larger design has confirmed. The class of temperature does not depend on that run, because its effect on aggregate holds in every model (@sec-class).
4. *Two outputs have no adequate model.* Acidic variants and fragments are judged on their measured results and set no range (@sec-criteria). For the acidic variants the reason is that the results carry no scatter, so the adequacy criteria cannot be applied, and the record gives no reason for that (@sec-centre). For fragments the reason is that the selected model predicts left-out runs much worse than it fits its own, which is a design of `{python} n_rsm` runs against an increase about `{python} fx(fr_ratio, 1)` times the repeatability of the method over the whole hold-time range studied. Neither attribute constrains the region of the step on the evidence available, and neither claim extends beyond the measured results. The verification of the fragment and acidic variant platform worst cases rests on those models, so neither confirmation is as strong as the aggregate one (@sec-verif).
5. *Three approaches were set after the results they judge.* The model selection of corrective action CA3 was adopted on `{python} ca3_date`, after the designs had been analysed. The approach to the hold study (@sec-hold) and the acceptance of the fragment bound of the confirmation runs (@sec-wc) were both decided once those results were known. Two rules were fixed before the results they decide, the clearance factors and the run counts of the cation exchange verification runs and of the confirmation runs (@sec-cex).
6. *The input pool of the designs was not tested.* The increase across the step that the verification needs is taken against the aggregate level of the load in the process model at set-point rather than against a measured load (PD-006-08).

The record of this report holds `{python} W(n_dev)` study events and `{python} W(len(PDS))` discrepancies from the plan (@sec-record). `{python} W(len(RE_STUDIES)).capitalize()` of the discrepancies are studies made during the re-analysis, each with what was planned, what was done and why.

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. The step meets its claim of `{python} fx(claim)` log~10~ of XMuLV clearance across the NOR in force, which is `{python} nor_t["ph"]`, `{python} nor_t["hold_time"]` and `{python} nor_t["temperature"]`. The lowest mean predicted log reduction in that NOR is `{python} fx(WC_X["predicted"])` log~10~.
2. The proven acceptable ranges are `{python} wu("ph", PARX["ph"])`, `{python} wu("hold_time", PARX["hold_time"])` and `{python} wu("temperature", PARX["temperature"])`. One edge of each is set by the clearance claim and the other is the end of the range studied, and each contains the NOR in force. Of the region studied, `{python} fx(100 * DSG["fraction"], 1)` % meets the criteria of the two outputs that have an adequate model.
3. Aggregate, fragments and acidic variants meet their intermediate acceptance criteria across the NOR in force, with the margins of @tbl-criteria-viral-inactivation, and the neutralized pool still meets them after `{python} H_DAYS` days at `{python} join_and(H_TEMPS)`. On material from the confirmation runs cation exchange cleared aggregate as the criteria assume and did not meet the rule for fragments, which was accepted on the risk PD-006-03 records (@sec-wc).
4. The scale-down model is qualified for aggregate and for acidic variants. Fragments and viral clearance were not compared at both scales. Their conclusions rest on the spiking model and on the cleavage reaction, as @sec-sdm sets out.
5. Inactivation pH is a CPP, hold time and temperature are WC-CPPs and A-Mab concentration is a GPP.
6. Within the NOR as characterized the step adds less aggregate than the platform worst case at the bound of a single batch, which widened the aggregate criterion of the production bioreactor output from `{python} fx(brx_tight)` to `{python} fx(brx_final)` % HMW. The platform values for fragments and acidic variants stand.
7. The tightest capability of the attributes this step changes is the acidic variant index of `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpk"])` against the lower end of its criterion, which the low-pH hold moves away from. Cumulative XMuLV clearance has an index of `{python} fx(CAPD.loc["lrv_xmulv", "Cpk"])`.
8. The record holds `{python} W(n_dev)` study events and `{python} W(len(PDS))` discrepancies from the plan. These ranges, classes and controls roll up into PCMR-001.

### DEV-006-01, hold-time record discrepancy between the control system and the manual log {.unnumbered}

During batch-record reconciliation the hold time recorded by the distributed control system (DCS) and the hold time in the manual log were found to differ by `{python} g(dev_006_01_time_discrepancy_min)` min. The root cause recorded is an offset between the clocks of the two records. Whichever record is right, the impact is bounded by the effect of the hold time on each output. A hold-time error of that size changes the predicted XMuLV log reduction by `{python} fx(dev1_x, 3)` log~10~, which is smaller than the residual standard deviation of its model, `{python} fx(FIT[X]["rmse"])` log~10~, and smaller than the margin of `{python} fx(WC_X["predicted"] - claim)` log~10~ at the least favourable NOR combination. It changes the predicted aggregate by `{python} fx(dev1_a, 3)` percentage points against a margin of `{python} fx(crit_agg - UPL_A)` points to the criterion. The record names no single run, so the event is assessed for the design as a whole. Every run was analysed at its design settings and retained in the analysis.

### DEV-006-02, cytotoxicity of the XMuLV infectivity assay at low dilution {.unnumbered}

The assay review found that the sample matrix was cytotoxic to the indicator cells of the XMuLV infectivity assay (AMV-3017) at low dilution, with the cytotoxicity recorded at a dilution factor of `{python} g(dev_006_02_cytotox_dilution)`. The root cause recorded is the matrix of the sample, and the record names no component of it. The record names no affected run either, so the event is assessed for the study as a whole. Wells that are cytotoxic cannot be read for infection, so the titre of an affected sample is read from higher dilutions, which raises the lowest titre the assay can report. A higher limit for the output titre can only make a computed log reduction smaller, never larger. Every run was retained in the analysis.

`{python} W(len(RE_STUDIES)).capitalize()` of them are studies made during the Version 2.0 re-analysis, after the results of the designs were known. They are PD-006-01, the study at the new pH set-point (@sec-ofat), PD-006-02, the cation exchange verification runs (@sec-cex), PD-006-03, the confirmation runs at the low end of the pH PAR (@sec-wc), PD-006-05, the hold study of the neutralized pool (@sec-hold), and PD-006-06, the clearance at the two ends of the concentration range (@sec-uni). PD-006-04 is the model selection (@sec-stats), which `{python} INV2["id"]` corrective action CA3 applies to every report of the campaign in place of the full quadratic model the plan prescribed, and the comparison of the models within 2 AICc units of each selected model is registered within it (@sec-near). The remaining two are requirements of the plan that were not met, `{python} PD_CONC` and `{python} PD_POOL`, and the two subsections below describe them.

What the model selection changed at this step is the following. The aggregate criterion of the production bioreactor output is `{python} fx(brx_final)` % HMW with the selection and `{python} fx(brx_agg_noca3)` % without it, because the verification bound of the cation exchange aggregate clearance comes from the selected model of that step (@sec-verif). The aggregate criterion of this step is `{python} fx(crit_agg)` % with the selection and `{python} fx(agg_wo_ca3)` % without it, for the same reason. The acidic variant criterion of the production bioreactor output is `{python} fx(brx_acid_ca3, 1)` % with the selection and `{python} fx(brx_acid_noca3, 1)` % without it. The comparison without the selection takes the bound of the full quadratic model of the acidic variants of this step, which reproduces its results exactly. An exact fit is never adequate, no model of that output of any form is adequate, and no bound of this step therefore replaces that platform value (@sec-verif). The bound this step contributes is nearly the same under either model of aggregate, `{python} fx(v_agg["predicted_nor_bound95"])` percentage points on the selected model and `{python} fx(bound_full)` points on the full quadratic. Every conclusion over the NOR, every proven acceptable range and both scale-down qualifications of this step are the same under the criteria the full quadratic models would have given.

### `{python} PD_CONC`, XMuLV clearance not measured in the concentration study {.unnumbered}

PCP-006 §6.4 required aggregate, acidic variants and the XMuLV log reduction on every run of the concentration study S-VI-UNI. The study measured aggregate and acidic variants only, because spiking had been scheduled for the designed studies alone and no titre was taken in the concentration study. The departure was found when the plan was compared with the study record during the Version 2.0 re-analysis, and Version 1.0 of this report did not notice it. The consequence was that the clearance across the concentration range had no result, while the range `{python} wu("protein_conc", rg(conc_lo, conc_hi))` was supported for aggregate and acidic variants alone. The confirmation study S-VI-UNI2 then measured the clearance at the two ends of the range in duplicate (PD-006-06). It detected no effect of the concentration, and with four runs it cannot exclude a loss at the high end of the range larger than the margin of `{python} fx(WC_X["predicted"] - claim)` log~10~ that the claim has over the NOR (@sec-uni). For XMuLV clearance the class of the parameter therefore rests on how the hold acts and not on the absence of a detected effect (@sec-class).

### `{python} PD_POOL`, input pool of the design runs not tested {.unnumbered}

PCP-006 §5.3 and §5.4 require a sample of the input pool, taken before acidification, on every run of both designs, tested for aggregate, acidic variants and A-Mab concentration. No input pool result is in the record of either design, because the input samples were not scheduled in the study record. The departure was found during the Version 2.0 review of the study record against PCP-006, after the designs had been analysed. The consequence is that the increase in an attribute across the step cannot be formed run by run. The verification of the platform worst cases needs that increase, and it is therefore taken against the aggregate level of the load in the process model at set-point, `{python} fx(FEED_AGG)` % HMW (@sec-verif). The A-Mab concentration of the design runs is likewise the value set and not a measured result (@sec-methods). Every criterion of the step is on the output of the step, so no judgement of an output against its criterion is affected, and every run was retained in the analysis.
